name: ETHICS AND SUFISM
synopsis: The course discusses the concept of Islamic ethics and Sufism and the importance of both towards human development. It also offers a discussion on the thought of Islamic ethics and Sufism by the Sufi figures and Sufism issues that arise in society. It also explores the practical aspects of the ta’dib method so that the students are able to practice Islamic ethics through the Sufism approach in everyday life and social responsibility to generate human capital excellence.

name: EVALUATION IN ARABIC LANGUAGE EDUCATION
synopsis: TBD

name: ISLAMIC ECONOMIC SYSTEM IN MALAYSIA
synopsis: This course aims to expose the student about the concepts of Islamic economic system and the main underlying institutions, the roles and operation of the Islamic economic institutions such as charitable institutions, financial institutions and regulatory institutions.

name: LANGUAGE IN SOCIAL CONTEXTS
synopsis: This course will introduce the basic principles of language usage in a variety contexts and situation. The students will be exposed to the context of use and usage of language for communication purpose.

name: STEM EDUCATION MANAGEMENT
synopsis: This course exposes students on how to use thinking as a tool to develop their cognitive abilities, embark on intellectual pursuits and build management competencies in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics) education. Students will study few topics related to STEM such as the different types of activities, experiments and their related applications. Students will also engage in the utilisation of DIY materials,and knowledge to address the lack of interest in STEM learning and management of STEM education in our country.

name: PHILOSOPHY AND CURRENT ISSUES
synopsis: This course covers philosophical relations with the Philosophy of National Education and Rukunegara. The use of philosophy as a tool to purify the culture of thought in life through the arts and methods of thinking and human concepts. The main topics in philosophy are epistemology, metaphysics and ethics discussed in the context of current issues. Emphasis is given to philosophy as a basis for fostering intercultural dialogue and fostering one's values. At the end of this course students will be able to see the disciplines of science as one comprehensive body of knowledge and related to each other.

name: MALAY LANGUAGE USAGE IN SOCIETY
synopsis: This course explains the basic concepts, applications and Malay language issues in community. In addition, this course will examine the history of the Malay language, politeness, and also the Malay language issues in areas such as social media, creative industry, administration, education etc. Besides providing opportunities for the students to interpret the Malay language issues in the society, this course also explores the correlation between language and culture in the community. Finally, the students will be able to understand and describe the use of the Malay language in the community.

name: MALAY LANGUAGE COMPETENCY
synopsis: This course discusses aspects of oral communication skills such as in lectures, speeches, briefings, and addresses. In written communication skills, we will discuss report writing styles, correspondence, memos, and various other related topics.

name: MALAY LANGUAGE IN MULTIMEDIA
synopsis: This course will introduce the concept of multimedia and information technology as a tool to enhance the use of the Malay language. The students will master the authoring applications to develop a software package that combines elements of interactive media in a single application. The students will also apply the authoring tools to produce a multimedia project suitable for the language industry.

name: LANGUAGE IN INTERPERSONAL COMMUNICATION
synopsis: This course will discuss concept, principles and characteristics of interpersonal communication and Johari’s model. Students will understand the differences in communication styles, body language and listening skill. Students will improve their communication skills through activities in two languages, namely English and Malay. Students will enhance their interpersonal skills through activities in class including conflict resolution, negotiation; and the relationship between organizational structure and communication process.

name: SOSIOLINGUISTICS
synopsis: Introducing concepts in sociolinguistics with a focus on the types of different languages factor, and diglosia.

name: E-LINGUISTIC
synopsis: This course trains students to generate ideas and apply their creativity through language skills in a medium of electronic resources. Students are also taught language strategies in presentation, commercialising and marketing through electronic mediums. This course will complement students' knowledge and skills in developing their own skills for career goals.

name: CORPORATE COMMUNICATION IN LINGUISTICS
synopsis: TBD

name: TRADITIONAL POETRY
synopsis: This course introduces the concept of a traditional Malay poetry verbal and written. This course also describes the genres of poetry written and spoken Malay. In addition, it displays the features, functions, and dissemination of traditional Malay poetry, and provide information about the elements of Malay intellectuals in traditional Malay poetry, and also it relations to the social, religious, educational, political, economic, and so on.

name: MODERN POETRY
synopsis: This course introduces the background, concepts and main principles in Modern Malay Poetry. The course also explains the historical background of literary history and the Malay literature criticism history from the earliest times to date. The course discusses the basic principles in comprehending and appreciating the aesthetical values and meanings of poems. Besides, it shows the relation between the local main issues and its implementation in poetry and gives info regarding major aspects that founded poetry writings in Malay World.

name: INTRODUCTION OF INTERNATIONAL LITERATURE
synopsis: This course introduces the genre and authors of world literature. The course focuses on selective of Islamic, China, Indian, Japanese and European Literature. This course aims to exposes the student to understanding the various themes of world literature from various periods and from various parts of the world in comparative contexts.

name: MALAY COSMOLOGY
synopsis: This course introduces how the Malays see and understand the world around them from the perspective of Anthropology. Basic concepts such as cosmology, world-view, local ecological system, and the invisible world is defined according to the Cultural Anthropology perspective. Each individual world-view of cosmological system of the Malay peoples is linked to their ties with the physical and invisible world. Explanations about the various Malay cosmologies are linked to the multiple Malay cultures and their adaptations to differing local ecological systems, as well as its associated invisible world.

name: ART, CULTURE AND MALAY SOCIETY
synopsis: Introduction to Malay music elements especially those containing Malay thoughts and aesthetics. Discusses music that has a load of such elements by appreciation and summarization going from traditional music to the more contemporary kind.

name: MALAY CIVILIZATION
synopsis: TBD

name: REGIONALISM IN EUROPE
synopsis: This course provides students with an overview of the history of European regionalism particularly the EU, and the legal, economic, and political dimensions of European integration. This includes the critical examination of current major problems in European integration and cooperation as well as options and perspectives for their solutions. The course relates the development of the EU to concepts such as good governance, regional cooperation, and global governance as well as to European political theory-building. The course includes fundamental debates within Europe, on concepts and issues of multilevel governance, regionalisation and inter-regionalism. In addition, it also touches on issues such as regional identity, values, and interests in both the intra-European aspects as well as the foreign relations of the EU.

name: MODERN EUROPE
synopsis: The course provides an examination of the historical transformation in the making of modern Europe. The aim is to provide students with a foundation on the conditions that gave birth to modern Europe. Emphasis is given to the major events in European history that paved the way for the making of a modern region. It offers insights into the ways in which national, regional and global dynamics interacted in the shaping of the European region.

name: THE MAKING OF MODERN SOUTHEAST ASIA
synopsis: The course provides an examination of the historical transformation in the making of modern Southeast Asia. The aim is to provide students with a foundation on the conditions that gave birth to Southeast Asia as a modern region. Emphasis is given to the major events in Southeast Asian history. The course covers topics such as early modernity, establishment of Western colonial rule, resistance to colonial authority, rise of nationalism, ending of colonial rule, establishment of independent states, and the birth of post-colonial states in the context of the Cold War. A key focus is on the efforts of Southeast Asians to shape their own destinies and establish their roles in the world. It offers insights into the ways in which national, regional and global dynamics interacted in the shaping of the region.

name: ASEAN AND REGIONAL SECURITY
synopsis: This course provides an in-depth assessment of the security challenges encountered by ASEAN member states since its establishment in 1967. The focus is also on the way ASEAN has managed regional security concerns through the cooperative security approach. The course covers a wide range of security issues, which include traditional and non-traditional security concerns as well as problems related to regional security cooperation. In addition, it also looks at the formation of the ASEAN Political Security Community and problems associated with its realisation.

name: ASEAN AND ECONOMIC INTEGRATION
synopsis: This course provides an assessment of the evolving economic issues in ASEAN economic cooperation and integration since its establishment in 1967. It covers a range of economic issues, focusing on the evolution of regional economic cooperation, and challenges related to the process of economic integration. In addition, it also discusses the formation of the ASEAN Economic Community and problems associated with its realisation.

name: DEVELOPMENT AND GOVERNANCE OF SMALL AND MEDIUM-SIZED ENTERPRISES IN ASEAN
synopsis: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in ASEAN have played a significant role in the generation of employment and in the overall inclusive and sustainable economic growth of the region. Nonetheless, SMEs here still face barriers that prevent them to harness their full growth potential. In order to remain competitive, the SMEs must adapt to the ever changing landscape of business, trade and technology. The course exposes students to different concepts, theories, policies and strategies pertaining to SME business and governance in ASEAN. It develops the knowledge of local conditions, business networks, e-trade, clusters, organisations and institutions beneficial for the growth of SME business. In addition, the students are also exposed to cross-cultural and inter-cultural aspect of managing the SMEs.

name: REGIONALISM AND REGIONALISATION
synopsis: This course begins by introducing students to theories and approaches to international relations before delving deeper into the theories and debates on regionalism/regionalisation. This includes covering the main contention surrounding the whole idea of old and new regionalism. It aims to present a systematic approach to the structures and dynamics of regionalisation models. In addition, the course also examines the main drivers of regionalism/regionalisation and how these are different between old and new schemes of regionalism/regionalisation.

name: INTRODUCTION TO ETHNOGRAPHY
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course aims to introduce ethnography as a key methodology to Socio-Cultural Anthropology. The course will be divided into two parts. The first part of the course will discuss ethnographic production. The second part focuses on basic concepts in ethnography, ethnography as a research methodology and the process of writing ethnographies.

name: SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course aims to provide extensive exposure to various issues closely related to sustainable development such as population growth, resource utilization, poverty eradication, lifestyle, environment, consumerism, and social inequality. This course also discusses the need to create a sustainable living environment in urban and rural areas. Also discussed is the sustainable development of the community or population of a country. Development-related theories are also discussed in an effort to help students understand sustainable development issues.

name: IDENTITY, DIVERSITY AND COMMUNITY
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course focuses on issues and problems associated with various forms of identities in the world community. Discussions cover issues related to social identity, inter-group contact and the concept of community in society. The course will also review the development of the concept of identity and community based on race, ethnic identity, gender and social class.

name: GERONTOLOGY
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course analyses changes in aging pattern of the population and its effect on economy ad demography. Development in health services has lengthened the age of the population which results in an increase in the percentage of elderly people in a society Thus, development should evaluate the elders’ needs so that they will not be isolated from modernisation and there will be no intergenerational crisis. Besides, students will try to evaluate the government’s policy on development of the elderly people. Active aging concept, if implemented will fulfil the needs in population changes.

name: PERSONALITY PSYCHOLOGY
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This subject covers a variety of personality theories including the theoretical and scientific explanations for individuals' characteristic patterns of perception, thought, emotion and behaviour. In addition, this subject also explores personality in applied contexts, such as choosing a career, developing personal relationships, and physical health.

name: FAMILY PSYCHOLOGY
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course gives a comprehensive understanding of the family as a dynamic social group that plays a vital role in shaping individual identity and behavior. Through a theoretical approach and interactive discussions, students will explore fundamental concepts such as family roles, mechanisms of family socialization, as well as the types and roles of families in various contexts.

name: INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE AND SCHOLARSHIP
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course will provide a groundwork for students on the history of the affirmation, development and legitimization of Indigenous knowledge, theory and scholarship in Malaysia and internationally. In investigating these knowledge structures students will learn about the diversity of Indigenous cultures in Malaysia.

name: PSYCHOLOGY OF HUMAN BEHAVIOR AND WORK
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course provides the basic knowledge of sustainable development principles in real estate development. It translates the abstract concepts of sustainability into tangible trends and cases to assist in understanding of sustainable real estate development including, but not limited to, the green building movement and city development concepts.

name: SOCIOLOGY OF DEVIANCE
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course aims to provide an overview of study of deviance and aspects of social control from various sociological perspectives. Discussion in this course will also covers aspects related to aberrations and deviations that occur in various aspects of human life (gender, class, sport, medical etc.) This course will also examine the various sociological approaches that attempt to understand deviant behavior that exists in society.

name: URBAN ETHNOGRAPHY
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: Students will be introduced to urban ethnography. The course is divided into two parts. In part one, students will learn about theory and key concepts in urban ethnographic research methods. In part two, students will be required to carry out a research project in the field for a period of 7 weeks. Students will be required to produce a research report.

name: HEALTH PSYCHOLOGY
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course introduces health psychology through learning about the theory and research finding related to psychological factors such as behavior, emotion, personality and so on. In this course also discussed the issues of health development, social psychology, and also the style of life that affects health.

name: GEOMORPHOLOGY
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: The thrust of this course is to explain the important aspects of geomorphology, the concepts of geomorphology, geomorphological systems and geomorphological equations. In addition, there should be a basic approach that preserves geomorphology as a study of the surface reaction as a result of applying shear stress forces to shear strength forces on the surface. This course will discuss why drainage basins are the most important geomorphological systems on the surface, how the relationship of energy and the generation of shear stress forces, how the characteristics of drainage basins regulate the shear stress forces and the resulting forms.

name: POPULATION GEOGRAPHY AND DEMOGRAPHY
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course will introduce students to the study of Demography and Population Geography. It will focus on factors that make spatial differences in the population component and the role of government in influencing of population patterns. Discussions in addition to the above aspects will also focus on current population theory and demographic changes.

name: GEOGRAPHY AND RESOURCE ANALYSIS
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: The course is divided into two parts. The first part discusses the relationship between Physical Environment, Natural Resources and Economic Development. The first part will also discuss why there are differences in time and space resource development. The discussion will also explain how differences ability to develop the natural resource of the country will set a progressive, developed and underdeveloped. The course will also discuss the relationship between key issues of the physical environment linked to co-building the natural resources. These issues are closely related to the changes to the natural process of the physical environment and issues related to waste. The first part will also discuss the concept of resource development “integrated Natural Resources Development” according Systems Drainage Basin as a unit of planning and development base. The second part will focus on issues related to human resource development, especially in the context of a developing country like Malaysia.

name: SOUTHEAST ASIA IN TRANSFORMATION
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course will identify explain and discuss all aspects of Southeast Asian geography. In-depth discussions would also be focused on physical geography of mainland, peninsular and insular of Southeast Asia. This course would also discuss issues and challenges common to the countries of Southeast Asia.

name: TECHNIQUES OF SOCIAL IMPACT ANALYSIS
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: The objective of this course is to expose students to the role of Social Impact Assessment in the implementation of development. Besides, the implementation of Social Impact Assessment will be explained and also examined regarding the importance of SIA towards achieving sustainable development. As well, the challenges of the Social Impact Assessment implementation will also be discussed.

name: ENVIRONMENTAL DISASTER GEOGRAPHY
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: The course examines how environment hazard and disaster can be classified. The course also explains the concept of human vulnerability to hazard threat and disaster. Students will be explained on the importance of hazard management.

name: URBAN PLANNING AND REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: The course has two main focus which are urban planning and regional development. Discussions will concentrate on development and the interrelationship between the two focus of these fields. This course will also study the distinct trends and patterns of development in urban and regional planning in different countries. The main theories in both fields will be studied and their effectiveness evaluated using case studies.

name: POLITICAL GEOGRAPHY
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course reviews the main theories and concepts underpinning political geography. By adopting spatial perspectives it will introduce a variety of theories and relates it to the processes of social and geographical change. Then, this course will concentrate on the formation of the states: the background, the system, its relationship with the other states and the challenges faced by the state in the ‘borderless world’ and ‘globalization’ process.

name: THE TWENTIETH CENTURY
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course serves to explore some of the important western literary and cultural trends of the 20th century. Modernist ideas and concepts will be studied by referring to the major works.

name: EFFECTIVE WRITING
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: TBD

faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: TBD

name: WOMEN AND LITERATURE
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: In this course, students will be introduced to a variety of literary texts by and about women. Students will discuss literary texts which will be grounded in various theories ranging from early feminist readings to more contemporary approaches. Students will learn how gender roles develop and change and how women’s views of themselves are reflected in their writing. Additionally, students will learn historical, philosophical and cultural information that will help increase their understanding and appreciation of the works.

name: LITERATURE OF THE RESTORATION AND THE EIGHTEENTH CENTURY

name: READING WORLD LITERATURE
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course will introduce students to the various ideas and texts that are considered as ‘world’ writing today. Some of the texts which can be dealt with include contemporary world poetry, Latin American magic realism, Franz Kafka, and contemporary graphic novels.

name: AGRICULTURE AND ENVIRONMENT
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: TBD

name: WEATHER AND CLIMATE
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course focuses on weather and climate systems in the regional and global scales. Students will be able to examine natural climate variability, their relationship with extreme weather events and their impacts on the weather. Students will be able to analyse the role of tropical weather systems, tropical climate variability such as El Nino, La Nina, Madden-Julian Oscillation, Indian Ocean Dipole on the weather and climate of Malaysia.

name: ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES AND CHALLENGES
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course introduces students to various environmental issues and challenges and how they relate to the ongoing social, economic, and political transformations of the modern world. Students will engage with key theoretical concepts and debates in environmental studies to help them analyse the causes, consequences, and potential solutions for the major environmental challenges of our time.

name: WATER RESOURCES MANAGEMENT
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course examines the occurance, management and conservation of water resources as it is a vital component for every society. This course capable to equip student with knowledge related to management of water resources in various aspect such as value chain, quality, monitoring, treatment as well as demand and uses. Students also will be introduced to current and emerging pollution in water resource issues, development, and technology.

name: CONSERVATION AND DEVELOPMENT
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course will introduce students to conservation movements and their links with development process. It covers development of conservation ideas and the conflict between conservation and development. Students will obtain the opportunity to evaluate conservation initiatives at the international level such as the National Park Initiatives and urban heritage conservation.

name: ENVIRONMENTAL DISASTER
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: The course examines how environment hazard and disaster can be classified. The course also explains the concept of human vulnerability to hazard threat and disaster. Students will be explained on the importance of hazard management.

name: SOCIAL MOVEMENTS AND DEMOCRATIZATION
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course is designed to introduce students to examine social movements and its relation with democratization process. The course covers the concepts, theories and impacts of social movements on world politics in transnational context. The students will be exposed on the impacts of globalization on the development of social movements, interaction between social movements and key political actors and the usage of media as a tool to increase the influence of social movements. The course will then expose the students on factors and processes that advancing or hindering the democratization process through case studies.

name: INTERNATIONAL LAW OF THE SEA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course exposes the students to the origins and evolution of the law of the sea and the sources of law applied by international courts and tribunals in resolving international maritime disputes. Emphasis is given on the 1982 Law of the Sea Convention (LOSC) which determines the rights, jurisdiction and duties of states within different maritime zones.

name: THE UNITED STATES IN WORLD POLITICS
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: TBD

name: POLITICS IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course will explain the impact of the legacy of tradition and colonialism on the developing countries. The concept of socio-political change, modernisation, nation-building and the process of democratisation and its attending challenges will also be identified. Contemporary political issues, the new international order, globalisation, neo-imperialism, domestic and international terrorism and their impact on the developing countries will also be given emphasis.

faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES

faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES

name: HUMAN RIGHTS AND INTERNATIONAL POLITICS
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course exposes the students to major human rights issues, encompassing violations of human rights and methods and efforts to deal with them. Emphasis is accorded to the imbalances in political and economic powers, and cultural differences between the East and the West, and the North and the South which have caused the differences in perceptions on human rights by both divides. Students are also exposed to various forms of human rights diplomacy adopted in international politics in influencing violators to change violation of human rights practices, and the effectiveness of such methods.

name: INTERNATIONAL DISPUTE SETTLEMENT
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES

faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES

name: POLITICS AND GOVERNMENT IN SOUTHEAST ASIA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: The course focuses on the political and administrative systems in Southeast Asia. The first part of the course is an introduction to the theories and concepts in politics. The course will also describe the background of the establishment of the state in the region. The impact of historical, cultural and geopolitical factors over the country's administration will be explained.. Focus will also be given on the political system and forms of government adopted in a few selected Southeast Asian countries. In the final part of the course, students are required to compare the political system and government of the countries in Southeast Asia.

name: PERFORMING ARTS OF SOUTHEAST ASIA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: Various social, economic, and political elements contributed to the formation and development of the performing arts in Southeast Asia. Throughout its development, the field of performing arts has been transformed into entertainment, employment, education, political agenda, and others by the community and the patron. This course is divided into three major parts; part one is an explanation of various theories and concepts related to performances and performing arts of Southeast Asia. Part two will identify the genre of the performances, traditional, modern, and contemporary, and its function in Southeast Asian society. Part three will analyse the role of the agencies, government, and international bodies in conserving and preserving main performances as national and world heritage.

name: CULTURE AND SOCIETY IN SOUTHEAST ASIA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: The course introduces students to socio-political cultures of communities in Southeast Asia with references to specific case studies from each Southeast Asian country. Key concepts related to socio-politics namely power, legitimacy, leadership and commonalities in the culture of Southeast Asian society will be discussed. Core religions namely Buddhism in mainland and Islam in island Southeast Asia as well as cultural practices and law such as the Adat among the people of the region will also be examined. The course also discusses adaptations to local socio-political cultures as a result of various external influences including Indian and Chinese civilizations, Islam and western colonisation. These consequently led to the multiple variations and syncretic practices and hybridization in the cultures of societies in Southeast Asia.

name: SOCIAL ENTREPRENEURSHIP IN SOUTHEAST ASIA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: Social entrepreneurship is a new and fast growing field of academic study and real world practice. In essence, social entrepreneurship is doing well financially by creatively solving social issues. This course introduces students to both theory and practice of social entrepreneurship through the use of innovative methods (including different products, foundations and organisations) to invoke action to practice, yield and sustain societal benefits. The course examines contemporary examples of socially entrepreneurial organisations, their benefits and limitations and their varied organisational structures and designs. Working in a team and on a social issue they care about, students will learn thinking skills, entrepreneurial mindset, leadership qualities and tools to start up their own social venture or work in a social business.

name: ETHNICITY, IDENTITY AND POLITICS OF MINORITIES IN SOUTHEAST ASIA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: The course will examine issues related to minorities in Southeast Asia in 3 parts. The first part introduces concepts related to politics of minorities in Southeast Asia. This will be followed with a discussion of issues, causes and various perspectives related to the politics of minorities through an examination of various case studies. The first category of case studies refer to ethnic and religious minorities such as the Karen and Rohingya (Burma), Malay (Thailand), Moro (Filipina), Cham (Vietnam) and Minahasa (Indonesia). The second category discusses indigenous minorities in Borneo and migrant minorities namely the Chinese and Indians in Southeast Asia, linking historical factors and the process of nation-state formation to their present status in Southeast Asian nation states. The third part focuses on conflict resolution by examining autonomy, partial sovereignty, legal recognition and other approaches for conflict resolution. Following this, the course evaluates existing state policies and role of international agencies in creating an inclusive and participatory environment for minorities in Southeast Asia. Towards attaining sustainable peace and inclusiveness of minorities in Southeast Asia.

name: HERITAGE OF SOUTHEAST ASIA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: Southeast Asia has a rich and unique cultural heritage. Tangible and intangible cultural heritage in Southeast Asia is a result of the creation and production of culture by Southeast Asian societies a few centuries ago. The recognition given by world organisations to tangible and intangible heritage in the world heritage list has enhanced the awareness of societies and governments in Southeast Asia in conserving, preserving and maintaining cultural heritage. This course is divided into four parts in which the first part will explain major concepts of heritages and traditions. The second part will describe the influential heritage and traditions in Southeast Asia. The third part will describe the policies and the role of governments of Southeast Asian countries in restoring and preserving heritages as well as continuing traditions in the region. The last part of the course will explain the role of various agencies in the implementation of programs to restore and preserve heritage as well as to continue traditions in Southeast Asia.

name: CULTURE AND SOCIETY OF JAPAN
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course introduces students to the patterns of Japanese culture and explores the fundamental characteristics of both traditional and modern Japanese society. Through topics such as philosophy, arts, food and beverages, language, ethics, manners, beliefs, and festivals, students will analyze and discuss the uniqueness and authenticity of Japanese culture and society, including historical perspectives, in collaboration with their peers. Additionally, students will develop digital skills and utilize digital materials to conduct research, present their findings, and engage in self-directed learning. Through group research projects, they will explore unique implications of Japanese culture and society. By the end of the course, students will demonstrate the ability to critically engage with diverse research effectively and navigate complex socio-cultural aspects.

name: CULTURE AND SOCIETY OF KOREA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This ia an introductory course to the culture and society of Korea focusing on South Korea. It provides an exploration of the multifaceted aspects shaping contemporary Korean culture and society. Students will examine and discuss everyday living of the Korean society including, but not limited to, their philosophy, family systems, religion and beliefs, customs, arts, pop culture, gender issues and the education system.

name: HISTORY OF CHINA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course offers a macro introduction to the history of China that dates from the Xia Dynasty to the Ming dynasty. Through the recurrent themes of unifications, fractures, prosperity and upheavals, the evolution of China from an ancient civilization into a dynastic empire provides the solid foundational background in understanding contemporary China's worldview.

name: POLITICAL ECONOMY OF CHINA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course introduces the political and economic structures of modern China since 1949. These structures are based on Marxist-Leninist ideology of the official Chinese Communist Party. From time to time, through the differences of eras, modifications and reforms have taken place. These changes are also covered in this course.

name: CURRENT ECONOMIC ISSUES IN CHINA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course concentrates on recent economic issues of China. Emphasis will be given on issues such as growth model, rapid and slow economic development, poverty, unemployment, rise of middle class, income gap, energy crisis, foreign reserve, corruption and others. Students will have the latest INFOation about developments and problems faced by China generally, especially current economic issues and the implications for the Malaysian economy.

name: NATION BUILDING IN JAPAN
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course examines how the formation of the modern Japanese state shaped the construction of the Japanese nation from the Meiji period to the present. It emphasizes key institutions such as the emperor, the constitution, the education system, the military, and state policies that influence national imagination. Students will evaluate the roles of political elites and state institutions in defining national membership and discourses of Japanese nationalism.

name: KOREAN CIVILIZATION
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course explores the deep-rooted influence of Chinese civilization on the development of Korean civilization, examining how cultural, philosophical, and political exchanges helped shape Korea’s unique identity. The course will begin by elaborating on the formation process of the Korean nation, tracing the historical foundations that led to Korea’s distinct national consciousness. Students will evaluate key aspects of Korean civilization—including philosophy, values, beliefs, economic systems, politics, culture, literature, and the arts—highlighting how these elements evolved over time. By the end of the course, students will gain a comprehensive understanding of the interplay between external influences and Korea's indigenous development, offering insights into Korea’s place in East Asian history and culture.

name: NORTH KOREA - SOUTH KOREAN RELATIONS
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: At the end of the course, students are expected to understand why the Korean peninsula became divided in terms of political systems and ideological orientations. The course includes discussions on inter-Korean relations, foreign intervention in reunification attempts, nuclear crisis and the security of the Korean peninsula.

name: FOREIGN POLICY OF CHINA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: At the end of the course, students are expected to understand why the Korean peninsula became divided in terms of political systems and ideological orientations. The course includes discussions on inter-Korean relations, foreign intervention in reunification attempts, nuclear crisis and the security of the Korean peninsula.

name: INTERNATIONAL TRADE AND INVESTMENT OF JAPAN
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: TBD

name: CONTEMPORARY POLITICS OF SOUTH KOREA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: The course examines the changes of South Korean structure and political institutions since the state’s inception in 1948. South Korean leadership in each era is evaluated and analyzed. The focus is to examine South Korea’s political democratization process and the result of civil society’s efforts in fighting for a democratic South Korean. The course also compares modernization and political democratization process between South Korea and other East Asian states.

name: INTERNATIONAL TRADE OF SOUTH KOREA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course provides a comprehensive overview of South Korea's international trade landscape, introducing students to fundamental theories of trade. It explores South Korea's trade policies from the 1960s to the present, examining the role of key organizations such as the World Trade Organization (WTO) and the impact of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs). The course also analyzes South Korea's economic relations with regional partners, including ASEAN, China, Japan, and the U.S., while discussing current trade issues that shape South Korea's position in the global economy.

name: INQUIRY INTO INDIAN CIVILIZATION
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course analyses various aspects related to history, social life, literature and science of Indian civilization from the early period to modern times.

name: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF INDIAN AND MALAY MODERN LITERATURE
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course explains the concepts related to the historical development of Indian and Malay literatures. An introduction about the theories of comparison will be given. Students will be trained to study the tests using the comparative literary theories. The thoughts based on culture will be taught.

name: EARLY CULTURAL CONTACT BETWEEN INDIA AND SOUTHEAST ASIA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course will expose students to a critical analysis on early cultural relationship between India and Southeast Asia. Chronological approach is used to show the continuity of 1500 years of (200 BC– 1300 AD) early cultural relationship between India and Southeast Asian countries. This period has witnessed cultural developments in terms of ideas, spiritual life, literature, arts, material culture and others. In general this course emphasizes on the lessons that one can learn from the early cultural relationship between India and Southeast Asian regions.

name: TRADITION OF INDIAN MUSIC AND DANCE
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: The aim of this course is to provide an introduction to the Tradition of Indian Music and Dance. Students will have an exposure to the basic principles of Indian Music and Dance. The unique characteristics of each art will be focused upon. Students will also learn the differences between the north and south Indian arts. The relationship between music and dance will also be analysed.

name: SEMINAR SERIES IN INDIAN STUDIES
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This series of seminar is intended to offer various insights of the Indian Society to students. Students will be given sufficient exposure to acknowledge the struggle, development and contemporary achievement witnessed by the Indians in Malaysia and outside of Malaysia. It will give significant emphasise to issues pertaining to Indian society and challenges facing by them in social, economic, politic dan culture. This will provide a platform for students to debate on contemporary issues pertain to Indian community.

name: GOVERNMENT AND POLITICS OF INDIA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course aims at explaining in detail and introducing the Indian government and political system. It involves the evolution of the Indian constitution and certain crucial aspects of the Indian constitution. The structure and system of Indian government and politics are discussed in the wide ambit of the Indian constiution. Also, this course discusses the relationship of the Indian state and central government. Apart from that, the main issues involving politics and government encountered by India are envisaged, elaborated and evaluated on the basis of acedmic principlesso that objective analysis and writing can be produced by students. On the whole, this course is expected to render effective input to students in order to comprehend the Indian government and political system based on academic principles and by means of this course, students are expected to write and response to the issues involving the Indian government an politcs based on objective analysis supported by academic approach and evidence.

name: CONTEMPORARY OF INDIA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course introduces the background and current status of contemporary India. Students will be exposed to contemporary social, economic and politic, and cultural development of India. Along this, issues pertaining to them also will be discuss in detail.

name: CHINESE CULTURE AND SOCIETY IN SOUTHEAST ASIA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course is an introduction to the historical, social and cultural experiences of the ethnic Chinese in Southeast Asia over the last two centuries. It begins with the patterns of early migration, settlement and evolution of Chinese communities before the formation of new independent nations. The second part of the course focuses on the role of Chinese in politics and economy of respective countries, and their varying responses and participation models. It also examines how the local context shape their identities and culture. Lastly, this course looks into the impact of globalization on the Southeast Asian Chinese.

name: STUDIES OF MALAYSIAN CHINESE COMMUNITIES
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course is a study of the Chinese society in Malaysia. It shows the diversity of Malaysian Chinese society and how it has been expressed in their language, religion, economic experience, localization process, etc. It focuses on the history of adaptations of the Chinese communities in local contexts and the continuity of Chinese culture. In addition, this course also discusses the varying responses of Malaysian Chinese in the recent socio-political development in Malaysia.

name: ECONOMIC ACTIVITIES OF SOUTHEAST ASIAN CHINESE
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: TBD

name: ANALYSIS OF CLASSICAL CHINESE TEXTS
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course will scrutinise four important Chinese classics. i.e. the Four Books which is made up of Daxue, Zhongyong, Lunyu dan Mengzi. Emphasis will be given to the content in terms of teachings, ethical value. Certain selected passages will be discussed in detail.

name: SELECTED NOVELS OF MING AND QING DYNASTIES
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course will be devoted to a careful reading of the masterpieces of Classical Chinese Novels in Ming & Qing Dynasty. Selected novels such as Sanguo Yanyi, Fengshen Yanyi, Shuihu Zhuan, Rulin Waishi, Jin Ping Mei, Laocan Youji, Xi Youji, Ernu Yingxiong Zhuan, Honglou Meng and Jinghua Yuan will be introduced to the students. It focuses on analysis and appreciation of the selected novel. Discussion on the writing skill, literature tradition and innovation will be conducted to expose the students to the important social & culture background in Ming & Qing Dynasty.

name: WELFARE SYSTEM
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: At the end of the course, students can: 1. Explain the meanings, functions, scope and theories of social welfare studies 2. Identify approaches, models and interventions in social welfare 3. Differentiate the processes in social welfare

name: BASIC HUMAN BEHAVIOUR
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course discusses the basic aspects of human behaviour. It includes the main approaches to understanding human behaviour, behavioural disorders, structure and dynamics of the group, and the social learning process. It also gives exposure to the students about the importance human behaviour in the interpersonal relationships.

name: ORGANIZATION BEHAVIOR
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course exposes students to aspects of management; such as models/approaches to organizational behavior, perceptions, values, attitudes and the importance of team in an organization. Students also will be given opportunities to learn about corporate social responsibility, leadership, effective communication, conflict/stress and the role of power/politic in an organization.

name: SOCIAL WORK WITH INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course exposes students to the basic generalist model of social work intervention as a method in micro level practice. The course introduces students to various situations, issues and theories in working with individuals and family. Basic knowledge and skills of the problem-solving approach, such as identification of issues and building rapport, case assessment, formulation of objectives, intervention, evaluation of outcome and termination are analysed. Students pursuing this course will also learn and examine the values and ethics in social work practice,which form the basic principles in social work services.

name: CRIME PREVENTION
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course provides knowledge and exposes students to the importance of crime prevention. Among the aspects that will be emphasized are the definition of crime prevention and an explanation of the levels in crime prevention. Students will also be exposed to various theories, programs, and crime prevention acts in Malaysia.

name: COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course exposes students to the generalist model in social work intervention at the macro level. Students will be introduced to a variety of situations, issues and theories in working with the community. Basic knowledge and skills to apply problem-solving approach in the community through the use of existing resources will be analyzed in detail. Students enrolled in this course will also have the opportunity to review the implementation of the assessment techniques of community development program.

name: HISTORY OF MODERN SOUTH ASIA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course will examine significant various historical developments in South Asia before and after 1947 with emphasis will be placed on political, social and economic history. Political history looking at administration, state elections, independent movement, political figures such as Mahatma Gandhi and Muhammad Ali Jinnah and so on so forth. Social history looking at relationship between various communities in South Asia particularly between the Muslims and Hindus, while in economic history, various aspects including trade, agriculture development and forestry will be discuss extensively

name: HISTORY OF MIDDLE EAST UNTIL EARLY 20TH CENTURY
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: The background of this course is the establishment, development and golden age of the Ottoman Empire as well as several Middle Eastern countries until the early 20th century. Focus of this course is the mid-19th century until the end of the First World War. encompassing discussions on Uthmaniyah, Iran, Egypt, and the emergence of the Arab nationalism movement. Discussions on the Ottoman Empire include the challenges faced by the expansion of Western powers, the transformation that took place, and the emergence of forces following the deterioration experienced by the central government. This course also discuss the transformation that has taken place in Iran and Egypt following the threat of the West and the reaction shown by the local community. Moroover, this course also discuss the role of Western influence in the development of Arab nationalism and the British conspiracy in the 1916 Arab revolt.

name: HISTORY OF INDONESIAN, 1900-1966
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course focuses on the course of Indonesian history from 1900 to 1966. The main themes are the change in the Ethics Policy and its impact on the development of Indonesian nationalism, the factors of the rise of Indonesian nationalism, the Japanese occupation and its impact on Indonesia, the development of post-war Indonesian politics, the process and negotiations of the transfer of sovereignty, the era of liberal democracy and guided democracy. The course discussion ends with the GESTAPU event in 1965.

name: NATIONALISM IN MALAYSIA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course aims to examine the existence of nationalist movements in the country, with a primary focus on the decolonization process after World War II. The basic knowledge that students will gain includes understanding the forms and patterns of nationalism that emerged in Europe, as well as the nationalist movements that developed in the country. This course covers the study of the Islah movement, socio-economic factors, association, and semi-political activities in the early stages of the country, followed by an analysis of major nationalist movements after World War II and their influence on the decolonization process. By the end of the course, students will be able to broaden their understanding of the role of nationalism in nation-building and prepare themselves to contribute to the social and political context of the country.

name: POLITICAL HISTORY OF THAILAND
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This thematic-based course discusses the development of Thailand history from the 1932 Revolution until the May Crisis, 1992. Among the themes discussed are the development of the institutional monarchy and its role before and after the 1932 Revolution, the role of the military and brureaucrats, as well as political parties in the development of Thai politics. Discussion includes the formation of Thailand political culture and how it affects the political process during this period. Emphasis will be placed on the series of Coup d’etat and the Thai election process from 1932 until 1992.

name: HISTORY OF INTELLIGENCE UNTIL 20TH CENTURY
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: Courses carried out on these specific themes will reveal some intelligence activities that play an important role in the war era. Various aspects of intelligence will be given attention as in the case of intelligence commencement as shown by The Art of War, Sun Tzu or Arthasastra, Kautilya. Additionally some themes about this activity will be given attention such as the involvement of certain figures and groups, propaganda, and so on during the Second World War era and beyond.

name: MODERN FILIPINO HISTORY
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course focuses on the last decade of Spanish colonization up to the advent of American occupation of the Philippines. The course begins with an introduction to important figures of early Filipino nationalism and the fall of the Spanish colonial government after the Spanish-American war. Then, this course will discuss in detail on the United States’ unique pattern of imperialism in the Philippines and the formation of a modern Philippines up to the independence in 1946.

faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: In this subject students study the scriptwriting process in the screen industry. They also will be exposed to the principles and techniques of script writing for various genres in the screen industry including television, film and digital media.

name: Persuasive Communication
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course addresses the communication processes that are intended to achieve specific persuasive goals in public speaking and campaigns. The application of this knowledge to the design of communication campaigns and interventions is also addressed. Particular attention is paid to communication through new media and technologies, including interactive, digital and social media, which are characterised by the integration of persuasive messages, entertainment and personalisation.

name: SELECTED CURRENT ISSUES
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course emphasizes the study of current issues in the Malaysian context. The focus is on the media's role in highlighting certain issues and its connections with national interest. Issues discussed include those related to politics, economy, education, social-issues, religion, culture, and the government administration.

name: COMMUNICATION MANAGEMENT
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course introduces the concepts, definition and strategies of comprehensive communication management within the Malaysian media sector. The course also dissects the techniques of message development, print and broadcast media vehicle selections. Students also learn the application of communication management techniques such as getting the client, pitching, client selection, agreement and job description using TOR, forming / managing client’s account and developing and designing communication strategies. By the end of this course students will be able to execute a comprehensive communication management for a media client.

name: MEDIA IN THE LOCAL AND GLOBAL CONTEXTS
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course explores how media operates within society, examining how it shapes, represents, and influences people in both local and global contexts while introducing foundational debates about media power, identity, representation, and cultural meaning. It then investigates the impact of globalisation on media industries, cultures, and audiences, analysing how global flows of information, technology, and cultural products influence local practices through issues such as convergence, cultural hybridity, and the tension between global forces and local identities. Finally, by comparing local and global media practices through critical evaluation and real-world case studies, students will develop the ability to identify how media systems differ across contexts and how these differences shape production, consumption, and representation, resulting in a nuanced understanding of media as a dynamic, interconnected field.

name: Political Communication
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course introduces students to a various basic matters related to political communication such as definition, process, approach, and how media plays it roles in this field. Students are given a general introduction to the world of political communication. This component includes an introduction to important concepts and principles in political communication as well as main issues such as campaign, political marketing and dynamism in political communication.

name: PUBLIC RELATIONS AND SOCIAL MEDIA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: The course will introduce a perspective on e-PR & the contemporary communication industry & the techniques & strategies used for high impact audience, managing organisation using PR and Social Media. The course also introduces discussion & evaluation of the usefulness of the Internet and Social Media for Corporate PR, PR Crisis, Community Relations, Investor Relations, Political PR, Political Personalities, Damage Control & Impact & Customer Satisfaction.

name: MAGAZINE PUBLISHING
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course introduces students to the principles and practices of magazine publishing in today’s digital-first media environment. It explores content planning, editorial processes, design, audience engagement, and multiplatform distribution, preparing students to develop and publish magazine content across print and digital formats.

synopsis: The course covers the following topics: Data Understanding and Interpretation: understanding the context and source of data to assess its reliability and relevance; Data Analysis and Critical Thinking: critical thinking skills to evaluate data findings and draw meaningful conclusions; Data Visualization and Communication; and Ethical Use of Data and Data Governance.

name: INFOATION PERSPECTIVES AND CONTEXT
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course provides an introduction to major themes and topics about INFOation, including INFOation entities and being an INFOation professional. Social, historical, ethical, legal, political, cultural issues surrounding INFOation creation, dissemination, use, control, and management are discussed as well.

name: DIGITAL REPOSITORIES
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course introduces students to basic concepts, principles, and technologies of digital repositories. They will also gain an understanding of metadata standards and how to practically apply them in organizing and managing digital resources. Furthermore, they will assess the effectiveness of digital repositories through the use of metrics and user feedback. Finally, students will design and implement access and retrieval mechanisms, including search interfaces and user authentication systems, for digital repositories.

name: DATA PRESERVATION AND METADATA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course provides an overview of methods for the preservation and long-term access to and utilisation of digitised and born-digital INFOation, including text, images, data, and audiovisual content. The following topics are addressed: the promise and challenges of long-term digital preservation and curation, the longevity of digital media, the integrity and authenticity of digital materials, the selection of digital materials for preservation, the formats and strategies for preservation, the preservation metadata, risk management, INFOation technologies that are relevant to the digital curation lifecycle, and the establishment of trustworthy digital repositories.

name: FUNDAMENTAL PROGRAMMING FOR DATA ANALYTICS
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course introduces students to fundamental Python programming for data analytics. Students will learn basic Python programming concepts, data structures, and control flow to solve data analytics problems. The course also covers the use of Python libraries such as NumPy and pandas for data manipulation, cleaning, and preprocessing. Students will learn how to analyze and visualize data using Python libraries like Matplotlib and Seaborn to gain insights and effectively communicate findings. By the end of the course, students will be proficient in using Python for exploratory data analysis, statistical analysis, and working with various data formats.

name: ADVANCED MEDIA AND COMMUNICATION THEORIES
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: The course introduces students to the three major theoretical perspectives in media and communication studies, namely the Positivist Perspective, the Interpretive Perspective, and the Critical/Cultural Perspective. The course then discusses several media and communications theories from each perspective. To clarify the association between theory and real world phenomena, students will be guided through the analyses of journal articles related to the theories and perspectives studied

faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course focuses on systematic explanations of the main ideas and concepts of Chinese Philosophy by referring to key philosophers and key texts of Chinese Philosophy. Major trends such as Confucianism, Taoism and Chinese Buddhism will be discussed. In addition, the course will also further analyse the development of Chinese Philosophy from the Pre-Qin era till modern day.

name: THE CHINESE SOCIETY IN SOUTHEAST ASIA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course examines the major concepts and theories in the studies of the Chinese in Southeast Asia. It discusses the application of these theories in the narratives of Chinese migration and adaption in the region in relation to its culture, colonialism, economic and political developments. This course also compares the diverse responses of Southeast Asian Chinese to recent socio-political developments. The last part evaluates the impacts of globalization, including the rise of China on the social development of Southeast Asian Chinese.

faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: The course covers the following topics: Introduction to information sources and services; the role of reference and information literacy service in the information environment; an analysis of user information needs and requirements; formulating research strategies, developing search skills, and evaluating information sources. It also provides students with the skills for conducting a reference interview and knowledge about ethics and legal liabilities of information provision.

name: INDEXING, ABSTRACTING AND THESAURI CONSTRUCTION
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course is an introduction to the nature and purpose of indexing and abstracting and the relationship of these topics in library and information disciplines. The course introduces core concepts in indexing, abstracting, information organization, and explores theories and methods for applying these skills, It provides the student with the necessary knowledge and skills to create and evaluate indexes and abstracts. It also integrates the study of indexing and abstracting into the larger field of library and information science such as information retrieval, databases, semantic relationship and metadata. Students will be exposed to techniques of thesaurus construction.

name: MEASUREMENT AND EVALUATION OF LIBRARY & INFOATION SERVICES
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course covers quantitative and qualitative evaluation tools, data analysis techniques, and service-specific evaluations, including technical services, reference, and interlibrary loan. Students will explore modern methods for assessing critical library aspects, user-centric, service-centric or product-centrics metrics. By the end, they will be able to apply evaluation tools, analyze data, improve service delivery, and communicate the library's value and other INFOation services.

name: BIBLIOMETRIC AND SCIENTIFIC PUBLISHING
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: The course covers the following topics: A survey of scholarly communication past and present with a particular emphasis on the changes in scholarly communication in the past ten years. Students will examine the interaction between society, technology and scholarly communication, the theory and practice of the communication of knowledge in academic and research environments, and how trends developments of scientific publishing and communication are affecting changes in scholarly communications. The course is concerned with the development, improvement, and interpretation of bibliometric indicators, in particular citation-based indicators for assessing research performance. Students will investigate and compare different data sources available for bibliometric analysis, such as Web of Science, Scopus, Dimensions, Lens and PubMed, and identify the major legal issues in terms of scholarly communication– including intellectual freedom, ethics considerations and the role of professional organizations and scientific community.

name: GENDER, MIGRATION AND DIASPORA
faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: This course connects contemporary trends in global migrations with a historical understanding of how and why migrants move, as well as how modern nation-states apply the logic of inclusion and exclusion on the basis of who has the potential to ‘belong’ as a participating citizen. The course is organized into key topics that attempt to unpack constructions of nations, borders, categories of legal and illegal migrants, the migrant body, all within the context of interrogating gender across and within borders. The course will also discuss a range of issues on gender, migrations and diasporas and will address the social and political dimensions of migration and diasporas as well as politics related to constructions of non/belonging. The goal of the course is to expose how today’s discourse of illegality and borders borrows from a longer history of state-sovereignty premised upon constructing – and excluding – the ‘other’.

faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
synopsis: In today's rapidly evolving digital landscape, understanding and effectively navigating digital technologies is essential for success in both personal and professional spheres. This introductory course aims to equip Undergraduate Level students with the fundamental knowledge and skills necessary to become digitally literate individuals by providing a comprehensive overview of digital technologies, their applications, and their impact on various aspects of life. Students will learn how to navigate the digital landscape, critically evaluate online INFOation, communicate effectively using digital platforms and tools, and explore topics related to digital INFOation and media literacy, digital communication and collaboration, digital safety and security, and digital content creation and productivity.

faculty: FACULTY OF ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
