name: DIGITAL SYSTEM
synopsis: An introductory course in digital logic circuits covering number representation, digital codes, Boolean Algebra, combinatorial logic design, combinational logic modules, and sequential logic circuits.

name: CIRCUIT ANALYSIS I
synopsis: This course introduces the fundamental theorems and analysis techniques for problem-solving in electrical circuits. It encompasses the techniques for analysing the DC and AC circuits, the transient response of RL and RC and RLC circuits, and the sinusoidal steady-state power calculation

name: ELECTRONIC CIRCUIT II
synopsis: Advanced amplifier analysis, including feedback effects. Frequency response. Design for power amplifiers, op-amps, analogue filters, oscillators and multivibrators.

name: BASIC ELECTROMAGNETICS
synopsis: This course gives an introduction to static electromagnetic fields. The student is first given a grounding in vector analysis. Then, electrostatics are introduced, with emphasis on electrostatic vector fields, electrical materials, capacitors and its derived energy and forces. Then, magnetostatics are given similar treatment regarding magnetostatic vector fields, magnetic materials, inductors and its derived energy, force and torque. Boundary value problems in static electromagnetics are also addressed.

name: APPLIED ELECTROMAGNETICS
synopsis: Starting with fundamental postulates of electromagnetism, Faradays law is introduced, leading to the discussion on Maxwell’s equations. The study of uniform plane wave includes the propagation of time harmonic plane wave in an unbounded homogeneous medium, the concept of pointing vector and the incidence of plane wave. Overview of the transmission lines will be explained. The general transmission-line equations can be derived from a circuit model, and the study of time harmonic steady-state properties of transmission line is facilitated by the use of graphical chart. Waveguides and basic of antennas will be explained.

name: CONTROL SYSTEM
synopsis: This course presents the basic knowledge of control system engineering. Topics covered include system modelling, the behaviors of linear time invariant systems in time and frequency domain, and design of simple controllers.

name: DIGITAL SIGNAL PROCESSING
synopsis: The definition of continuous time (analogue), discrete time and digital signals, Fourier series and Fourier Transform is discussed. The discrete time linear time-invariant (LTI) signal processing systems and the application of the time-domain convolution and the Discrete Time Fourier transform (DTFT) in analyzing LTI systems are also discussed. The design of FIR digital filters and introduction to z-transforms and IIR type discrete time filters are covered in detail. The Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) and the implementation of the DFT by the fast Fourier Transform is also covered

name: POWER SYSTEM
synopsis: This course will prepare students with the fundamental knowledge on electrical power system analysis. In-depth knowledge of the modern theory, design and practice of electrical power systems will be provided in this course. Four types of most important power system analyses will be taught that are: load flow, fault, protection system and transient stability. All of these analyses are used in practice for planning, design and operation of a power system.

name: STATICS
synopsis: The course aims at introducing the student to the field of mechanical engineering – solid mechanics. The student will learn to analyze forces acting on particles and rigid bodies in static equilibrium which involve problems in 2D and 3D. The students will be exposed to conceptualize, design, build, and test a load-bearing device or structure.

name: FLUID MECHANICS 1
synopsis: The goal of this course is to impart knowledge, understanding and an appreciation of the field of fluid mechanics. This course includes the study of the basic properties of fluids which encompasses both gases and liquids, the basic concepts of system, control volume and flow field, the basic principles of conservation of mass, energy and momentum, the fundamental equations that govern the behavior of fluids, the application of the principles and equations to the understanding of the operations of various types of flow measuring equipment and the study and analysis of the forces that act on bodies moving through a fluid and vice versa

name: ENGINEERING MATERIALS 1
synopsis: This course focuses on atomic structure, bonding between atoms and crystalline and imperfections in solids. The relationship between the microstructure and mechanical properties of metals as well as strengthening mechanisms will be discussed. Using the phase diagram, microstructure development and alteration of mechanical properties of metal and non-ferrous alloys will also be described

name: ENGINEERING DESIGN AND MODELLING
synopsis: In this course, students are taught techniques for graphics communication and to develop a standard engineering drawing by sketching and by using a CAD software. This course covers sketching techniques, engineering geometry and 3D modelling, multi-views and visualizations such as multiviews drawing of an object, auxiliary views, pictorial projections and section view, the practices of geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GDT) in engineering drawings. Finally, students will learn the techniques for assembly drawings of a complete product.

name: MECHATRONICS 1
synopsis: The course introducing students electrical elements such as resistor, capacitor and inductor that are used in the basic electric circuit. Sfunctions and interconnection discussed covering direct and alternating current circuit. Theorems such as Kirchhoff's Voltage Law and Kirschhoff's Current Law are among the theorems exposed to solving problem to obtain current, voltage and power. Apart from that relationship between electric and magnet (ie electromagnet) structure is also covered in this course. These basics will direct to the understanding of the design and aplications of motor and generator.

name: COMPUTER PROGRAMMING
synopsis: This course introduces students to computer systems and makes them familiar with the computer programming. The course helps students to develop their skill and feel confident to write computer programs and map scientific problems into computational frameworks.

name: FLUID MECHANICS 2
synopsis: The aim of this course is to further the knowledge and understanding acquired in the basic fluid mechanics course given in the first year. This course includes mainly the application of the understanding acquired to the analysis of various phenomena encountered in the very broad field of fluid mechanics. Such pehnomena include the flow of fluids in pipes, the study of the lift and drag forces acting on bodies immersed in a fluid, the study and analysis of flow through turbomachines, such as pumps and turbines and the applications of the laws of similarity and dimensional analysis.

name: MECHANICS OF MATERIALS 2
synopsis: This course focuses on analyzing stresses and deformations in materials under load. Various types of loads are investigated including axial loads, torsion, bending and transverse loads. Basic concept of stress and strain transformations will also be discussed.

name: PRODUCT DESIGN AND INNOVATION
synopsis: Product Design and Innovation is a unique course developed to prepare the students to design products and develop technologies for current and future needs. This course is a project-based course that covers modern tools and methods for product design and development. The cornerstone is a project in which teams of management, engineering, and industrial design students conceive, design and prototype a physical product. Class sessions are conducted in workshop mode and employ cases and hands-on exercises to reinforce the key ideas. Topics include identifying customer needs, concept generation, product architecture, industrial design, and design-for-manufacturing.

name: INSTRUMENTATION AND MEASUREMENT TECHNIQUES
synopsis: The course is aimed at exposing the students the classical and current instrumentations and measurement techniques applied in industries. The course discusses the application and principles of transducers and data acquisition, postprocessing and documentation. The advantages and disadvantages between measurement techniques and computational method are highlighted.

name: MECHANICAL VIBRATIONS
synopsis: This course is aimed at introducing the fundamentals of vibrations for single degree of freedom (DOF) systems, 2 DOF systems in engineering field. This includes undamped and damped with free and forced vibrations for translational and rotational system. It also includes application for vibration isolation, control and vibration measurement.

name: ENGINEERING MATERIALS 2
synopsis: This course focuses on the structures-rightful of engineering materials. It’s includes the crystal structures, phase diagram, precipitation, deformation and others related mechanical properties. Then, introduction on the mechanisms in engineering materials such as mechanisms of dislocation, diffusion, deformation etc. Macroscopic and microscopic structures and the rightful of materials in engineering application are discussed. Interpretation and relation between materials, mechanism, and application in real life are explained and analyzed.

name: PRODUCTION AND OPERATIONS MANAGEMENT
synopsis: Operations Management is one of the primary functions of a firm, focusing on the activities of producing and delivering products or services. This course will expose students to the aspect of designing, analyzing and improving the whole transformation process, including procurement, production and distribution, with the objective of creating advantage for the company. The objective by the end of the course is to provide student with the analytical skills and managerial insights necessary to critically analyze a firm's operations decisions and practices.

name: CHEMICAL PROCESS PRINCIPLES I
synopsis: This course first reviews the use and propagation of significant digits. It is followed by introduction to the key systems of units in engineering, including inter-conversion of units. This leads naturally to the major quantities encountered, including ways to estimate (e.g. ideal gas density) or to obtain them (e.g. solubility). Use of advanced thermodynamics for prediction is NOT required. The basic features of key unit operations will be clarified mainly to enable students to identify the typical nature and number of streams associated with each. The focus then shifts to the derivation of the general mass balance equation. This is followed by single unit, non-reactive, steady state mass balance. The use of degrees-of-freedom analysis will be illustrated. Introductory unsteady state problems will illustrate the more general use of mass balance. Complications involving gaseous streams, single and multiple chemical reactions, chemical equilibria, physical equilibria, Lever Rule will be introduced in stages. Multiple unit operations will appear in between. The necessity and the proper way to summarize the results with a PFD will be highlighted. The three basic configurations of bypass, recycle and purge, in the presence of complications listed above, will be thoroughly covered until the end of the course.

name: MASS TRANSFER
synopsis: This course first introduces mass diffusion and flux, leading to Fick’s Law and the diffusivity. The Fickian constitutive equation will then be incorporated into the material balance to arrive at the general mass transport equation. Various important scenarios amenable to analytical solution such as diffusion in a stagnant gas film, equimolar diffusion, diffusion with reaction will be examined. With these established, basic experimental methods of evaluating the diffusivity will be covered. For more complex situations including boundary layers and multiphase flows, the concept and application of convective mass transfer coefficient are introduced. This is again followed by discussions on experimental techniques to determine the mass transfer coefficient. For cases with no empirical data, use and misuse of analogies are examined.

name: FLUID MECHANICS II
synopsis: The course will begin with the integral linear momentum balance concepts and applications. This is followed by stresses due to fluid motion and the stress tensor for compact representation. The extended Divergence Theorem or the differential linear momentum balance enables conversion into the differential form, i.e. Cauchy’s First Equation of Motion. Application of constitutive equations leads to the Navier-Stokes equations. Discussions on boundary conditions for analytical solutions of Navier-Stokes equation will follow. Sample problems for analytical solutions will be covered for various simple flow problems. Finally, fundamental of CFD and software packages for numerical solution will be introduced to handle more complex problems.

name: SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN ENGINEERING
synopsis: The course begins with a re-capitulation of the role of engineers to operationalise the sustainable development concept. To connect the biotic and abiotic spheres, the ecosystem structure, function, material and energy flows will be covered. Next the impact and contribution from industrial activities to air, water and soil media is discussed together with impacts due to energy utilization and resource depletion. Identification and quantification of these impacts via EIA as currently practiced will follow. This leads to more advanced concepts associated with green engineering/ green design together with the resulting assessment frameworks and indicators. The tricky issue of balancing economics against the environment is then addressed. The perspective widens further to encompass the social dimensions of sustainability, in particular the roles and involvement of corporate citizens. In this globally interconnected world, all these techno-socio- economic measures come under the umbrella of the relevant statutes and international treaties or trade blocks. The engineer must also know how to strive for sustainable development within these regulatory frameworks. To achieve learning outcomes more effectively, students are exposed to various sustainability development activities inside and outside the University of Malaya campus as well as participate in sustainability program.

name: NANOTECHNOLOGY FOR ENERGY CONVERSION AND STORAGE
synopsis: TBD

name: BIOINSTRUMENTATION
synopsis: This course covers the principles, technologies, methods and applications of biosensor and bioinstrumentation. The objective is to link engineering principles to understanding of biosystems in sensors and bioelectronics. Instrumentation amplifier and the bridge circuit will be covered in detail. The transduction principle based biosensor systems will also be discussed extensively. The students will be able to design and select the appropriate components in response to measurement problems.

name: ENGINEERING BIOMECHANICS AND MOTION ANALYSIS
synopsis: This course introduces fundamental biomechanics concepts for human motion analysis, focusing on multi-segment rigid body systems. Students will learn methods for analyzing and solving equations of motion for these systems in biomechanical applications. The course also covers the structure and function of the musculoskeletal system, integrating anatomical and physiological principles to understand human movement mechanisms. Computational modeling techniques and musculoskeletal biomechanics are applied to simulate and evaluate human movement dynamics in various contexts, including sports, medicine and rehabilitation engineering.

name: HEALTHCARE TECHNOLOGY
synopsis: In this course, students will learn an in-depth exploration of healthcare technology with a focus on medical devices for continuous health monitoring. The medical devices covered in this subject shall encompass sleep assessment, human motion biomechanics, therapeutic devices, and interventional devices. It covers the fundamental principles of medical device design, physiological measurements, and the application of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare. Students will gain hands-on experience with wearable sensors relating to sleep assessment and human movement analysis. Additionally, the regulatory, compliance and biasing aspects shall be covered in this course. Through hands-on activities, projects, and case studies, students will apply data analytics techniques to healthcare applications, analyze real-world data, and develop innovative solutions for healthcare medical technology. The course also explores emerging trends and entrepreneurial opportunities, preparing students for careers in healthcare technology, biomedical engineering, and medical device innovation.

name: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN MEDICINE
synopsis: The course covers the fundamental understanding of the artificial intelligence concepts and its basic applications in biomedical engineering.

name: SAFETY, STANDARD AND ETHICS IN BIOMEDICAL ENGINEERING
synopsis: The course covers the medical device regulation and regulatory bodies and demonstrates the international and national medical devices regulation, safety and standards. The electrical safety and tests in Medical devices are also explained. Design calculations for electrical safety of medical devices. Guidelines for of safe medical devices , medical instruments, electrical accidents , eg micro and macro shocks , electrical physiological effects to humans ,leakage current , and devices to protect against electric shock. Industrial in production of analyzing the safety testing of medical devices used in hospitals such as ECG machine. The course also covers ethical and bioethical issues related to biomedical engineering.

name: MACHINE LEARNING
synopsis: To provide students with an in-depth introduction to two main areas of Machine Learning: supervised and unsupervised. Some of the main models and algorithms for regression, classification, clustering and Markov decision processes will be discussed and studied. Topics will include linear and logistic regression, regularisation, MLE, probabilistic (Bayesian) inference, SVMs and kernel methods, ANNs, clustering, and dimensionality reduction.

name: DATA ANALYTICS
synopsis: This course aims to provide the students with basic concept of data analytics, focusing on the electrical engineering applications. Among the topics that are covered in this course are various techniques for data preparation and modeling, decision-making, data classification and data clustering. Besides, tools used for data analytics is also introduced in this course, including Python and R Programming, and Hadoop.

name: SYSTEM ANALYSIS AND DESIGN
synopsis: This course introduces a core set of skills that all analysts need to know no matter what approach or methodology is used to develop more effective and efficient systems. All information systems projects move through the four phases of planning, analysis, design, and implementation. All projects require analysts to gather requirements, model the business needs, and create blueprints for how the system should be built; and all projects require an understanding of organizational behavior concepts like change management and team building.

name: SMART POWER DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM
synopsis: This course introduces important concepts in power system. The course also provides in-depth knowledge on the distributed generation and low carbon technology as well as the impacts and challenges of its integration into modern distribution networks. Students will learn how to design appropriate solutions for distribution system planning to satisfy national and international electrical distribution standards in anticipation of future smart grid concepts.

name: POWER ELECTRONICS
synopsis: This course presents power electronics applications, EMC standards, DC-DC switch-mode converters, PWM techniques, three-phase buck, boost and flyback converters, resonant converters and multilevel inverters.

name: DIGITAL SIGNAL PROCESSING
synopsis: This course presents a broad-based introduction to digital signal processing system design and a solid grounding in theory and techniques which can be applied in various engineering applications. Topics covered are analogue to digital conversion process, digital filters, Laplace transform, Z-transform, hardware and software for digital signal processors, and applications of digital signal processing to process image and audio signal.

name: COMMUNICATION NETWORKS
synopsis: This course is designed to provide an in-depth study on communication networks and their supporting technologies. It covers the evolution of networking technologies from circuit switching to packet-switching networks, and how these networks are used in supporting various types of applications, such as VPN and MPLS. Besides, network security is also introduced.

name: MEMS DESIGN
synopsis: MEMS are miniature devices in micron dimensions that are capable of performing many tasks and functions that involve electrical, mechanical, thermal, optical, fluidic, and other types of signals. This course will provide the fundamentals from many disciplines relevant to the understanding and application of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS) technology. Design topics will include mechanical, RF and microfluidic principles. Fabrication methods will cover bulk and surface micromachining techniques that rely heavily on VLSI processing. Process integration with existing device platforms and materials properties related to MEMS design and fabrication will be discussed.

name: DISCRETE-TIME CONTROL SYSTEMS
synopsis: This course deals with the theory and the design of discrete-time control systems. Major topics include Z-transform, sampling and data reconstruction, performance and stability analysis of discrete-time systems and design of digital controller using frequency response based and state-space based techniques.

name: HUMAN-COMPUTER INTERACTION
synopsis: This course explores the fundamental principles, theories, and applications of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), based on the book "Human-Computer Interaction" by Alan Dix, Janet Finlay, Gregory Abowd, and Russell Beale. The course focuses on user-centered design, interaction models, and usability evaluation techniques to create intuitive, efficient, and accessible digital systems. Key topics include usability principles, heuristic evaluation, interaction paradigms (GUI, voice, touch, multimodal interfaces), and emerging technologies AI and enhancing user experience efforts. Ethical, social and legal implication of HCI are also explored for further consideration.

name: INTELLIGENT HEALTHCARE SYSTEM DESIGN
synopsis: This course introduces the principles and applications of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the design of healthcare systems, emphasizing on systems engineering concepts such as signal processing, electronic sensors, medical imaging, and embedded systems to enable AI-driven healthcare solutions. It explores AI techniques such as machine learning and deep learning to enhance clinical decision-making, automate diagnostics, personalize treatment, and improve operational efficiency in healthcare systems. The students wil learn to integrate AI embedded hardware systems and also include optimization strategies in machine learning models for efficient hardware realization. By the end of the course, students will be able to design, implement, and evaluate AI-based solutions in systems engineering for various healthcare applications while understanding their ethical and societal impacts.

name: OCCUPATIONAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH IN ENGINEERING
synopsis: In this course, students will be able to learn about the occupational health aspects important to the industry, inclusive of health hazards, occupational health laws, occupational disease, occupational hygiene and prevention of health hazards at the workplace.

name: SUSTAINABLE PROCESS ENGINEERING
synopsis: This course will introduce the students to general issues in environmental pollution, properties and fate of environmental contaminants, transport and transformation of contaminants and industrial activities and the environment. Moreover, the students also will be exposed to the sustainable process development and design, sustainable process operations, integrated pollution management, regulations and international commitments as well as the sustainable development.

name: HAZARD IDENTIFICATION AND EVALUATION
synopsis: This course will introduce students to the Hazard Identification Techniques such as hazard survey (Checklist), Job Safety Analysis, Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment Control (HIRAC), HAZOP, Fault Tree Analysis as well as Safety Audits, Hazards from Chemical Reaction, BLEVE, VCE, Safe Handling of Industrial Chemicals, Flammability Limits for Vapor, TLVs and Explosion. Furthermore, students also will be able to learn about Designing for Safety, Process Safety Management, Performance Standards for a Safety Improvement Process, Safety Attitudes and Human Behaviour, OSHA 1994, CIMAH, Accident Cost Estimation, Accidents Review and Analysis and Accident Investigation Study.

name: LIFE CYCLE ASSESSMENT AND MANAGEMENT
synopsis: This course will introduce students to Environmental Issues and Management, Life Cycle Based Environmental Initiatives, ISO 14040 – Introduction to Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) Series of Standards Goal and Scope Definition, Life Cycle Inventory, Life Cycle Impact Assessment, Life Cycle Interpretation, SIMA PRO – LCA simulation software and LCA course Project. Besides, students also will be exposed to the Life Cycle Management (LCM), LCM Tool Box, Environmental Management Systems, Integrated Chain Management, Management Approaches Toward LCM and Challenges for Developing Countries.

name: INDUSTRIAL ERGONOMICS
synopsis: This course contains eight essential parts mainly: industrial safety and health, ergonomics industries, ergonomics principal in design, effect of environment on workers, human physiology, anthropometry, works design and analysis of tasks.

name: AIR POLLUTION MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL
synopsis: This course will introduce students to general issues on air pollution, air quality and also types, sources and impacts of air pollutants. Besides, students also will be exposed to the Global warming issue, air meteorology and dispersion of pollutants, as well as management and control of gaseous and particulate air pollutants.

name: OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH AT WORKPLACE
synopsis: In this course, students will be able to learn about the occupational health aspects important to the industry, inclusive of health hazards, occupational health laws, occupational disease, occupational hygiene and prevention of health hazards at the workplace.

name: GREEN INDUSTRIES: SUSTAINABLE PRACTICES AND TECHNOLOGIES
synopsis: In this course, students will develop a comprehensive understanding of sustainability concepts and their relevance in industrial settings, with a focus on applying these principles to chemical, manufacturing, and energy sectors. Students will learn to design and optimize sustainable industrial systems, utilizing green engineering principles to enhance process efficiency, minimize waste, and improve resource utilization. The course will also train students to conduct impact assessments with a focus on environmental considerations such as carbon footprints, waste production, and resource consumption. Students will propose actionable green solutions to mitigate these impacts in industrial operations.

name: INNOVATIVE ERGONOMICS FOR TECHNOLOGY DRIVEN INDUSTRIES
synopsis: This course contains eight essential parts mainly: industrial safety and health, ergonomics industries, ergonomics principal in design, effect of environment on workers, human physiology, anthropometry, works design and analysis of tasks.

name: LIFE CYCLE ASSESSMENT: PRACTICES FOR SUSTAINABLE INDUSTRIES
synopsis: This course will introduce students to Environmental Issues and Management, Life Cycle Based Environmental Initiatives, ISO 14040 – Introduction to Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) Series of Standards Goal and Scope Definition, Life Cycle Inventory, Life Cycle Impact Assessment, Life Cycle Interpretation, SIMA PRO – LCA simulation software and LCA course Project. Besides, students also will be exposed to the Life Cycle Management (LCM), LCM Tool Box, Environmental Management Systems, Integrated Chain Management, Management Approaches Toward LCM and Challenges for Developing Countries.

name: MANAGEMENT AND TECHNOLOGY IN AIR POLLUTION CONTROL
synopsis: This course will introduce students to general issues on air pollution, air quality and also types, sources and impacts of air pollutants. Besides, students also will be exposed to the Global warming issue, air meteorology and dispersion of pollutants, as well as management and control of gaseous and particulate air pollutants.

name: CRISIS AND EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT IN EMERGING INDUSTRIES
synopsis: This course equips participants with the skills and knowledge necessary to effectively manage industrial crises and emergencies. Through an in-depth exploration of hazard assessment, risk analysis, and vulnerability identification, participants will learn to apply industry-specific frameworks and methodologies to proactively mitigate potential threats. The program emphasizes the design and evaluation of comprehensive crisis management plans, ensuring that both short-term and long-term impacts are addressed. Key components include the integration of organizational resources, stakeholder coordination, and adherence to regulatory requirements. Additionally, the program focuses on evaluating crisis management responses through real-world case studies, enabling participants to identify lessons learned and areas for improvement in industrial emergency management systems. By the end of the program, participants will be prepared to lead strategic initiatives aimed at preventing, responding to, and recovering from industrial emergencies.

name: ENGINEERING DATA ANALYTICS
synopsis: Data-driven decision making process is an essential component of emerging engineering systems in industry 4.0. It mainly involves effective data featuring task and discrete system modelling skill. This course introduces general mathematical tools used to analyse engineering data such as numerical analysis and signal processing, in order to extract its suitable feature for prediction of the desired outcome. Students need to develop a mathematical model or a ‘black-box’ model with machine learning, and apply it with the selected data feature to estimate the solution. Hence, this solution will give a new insight for better decision making in engineering application.

name: THERMAL SYSTEMS ENGINEERING
synopsis: Thermal resistance network for steady heat transfer, Steady heat transfer from finned surfaces or heat exchanger, Transient heat conduction in uniform and standard geometries and with spatial effects, Fluid flow and heat transfer over flat plate, cylinders and sphere and ove tube banks, Laminar and turbulent flow and heat transfer in tubes, Numerical Method and Computational Fluid Dynamics (2D & 3D cases), Heat exchangers, Radiation Heat Transfer.

name: ENERGY CONVERSION AND STORAGE
synopsis: Introduction to energy, Energy scenario, Energy economics, Heat Engines & thermodynamics: fluid power and heat engine, Heat Engines & thermodynamics ;thermodynamic processes and properties, Thermal to mechanical energy conversion: Rankine Cycle, Chemical to thermal energy conversion - Fuels & Combustion, Thermal to mechanical energy conversion- Brayton cycle, Nuclear to Thermal Energy Conversion, Electromagnetic to Thermal Energy Conversion- Solar, Electromagnetic to Electrical Energy Conversion- PV, Chemical to Electrical Energy Conversion- Fuel Cells, Energy efficiency improvement, Energy Storage

name: COMPUTATIONAL FLUID DYNAMICS
synopsis: The course will provide students with a sound understanding of the use of computational simulation and modeling techniques applied to engineering problems. It will also provide insight into advanced data structures, algorithms and software design. An introduction to distributed and high performance computing methods will also be included.

name: HVAC AND BUILDING ENERGY MANAGEMENT
synopsis: Understand the design principles for air conditioning and refrigeration apparatus. Evaluate the operation of air conditioning equipment under varying load conditions. Develop the ability to use information from established design handbooks such as the ASHRAE guide. Be able to perform building air conditioning load calculations and appreciate factors influencing them.

name: MATERIALS SELECTION IN MECHANICAL DESIGN
synopsis: This course starts with a review of the structure and properties of major families of materials as well as a review of the engineering design process. It then introduces performance criteria and materials property charts. Basics of materials selection process in engineering design are covered. Students will be trained to select materials in complex design situations involving multiple constraints and conflicting objectives. Economic and environmental factors are discussed.

name: INTEGRATED COMPUTER AIDED DESIGN IN PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT
synopsis: This course emphasis on parametric solid modelling using commercial computer aided design software. Student is expected to develop skills and utilize appropriate techniques to produce geometric profiles that serve as a database to produce 3-D models, working drawings, bill of materials and exploded views of assembled models. In addition, the student will be exposed into development of rapid prototype output (3-D printing) and advanced technology of augmented reality (AR).

name: TRAFFIC ENGINEERING AND SAFETY
synopsis: TBD

name: URBAN TRANSPORT PLANNING AND SAFETY
synopsis: This course introduces the influences of urban planning policies on susceptibility to urban and road traffic risks; urban streets concerns and their functions, essential principles for forming urban traffic safer for pedestrians, bicyclists, and public transport users; different techniques to explain and evaluate the traffic crashes.

name: RESEARCH METHODOLOGY FOR COURSEWORK
synopsis: This course offers a thorough overview of the fundamental principles and methods of conducting research in engineering disciplines. Students will be exposed to a variety of research methodologies, such as mixed-method, quantitative, and qualitative approaches, with a particular emphasis on scientific research methods. Students will investigate the fundamentals of research design, data acquisition methodologies, and ethical considerations in research at the commencement of the course. They will acquire a comprehension of the significance of integrity in scholarly work, responsible conduct of research, and research ethics. Furthermore, the course will provide students with the opportunity to employ appropriate methods for data interpretation and validation by covering experimental design and statistical analysis techniques. In addition, students will acquire the ability to critically evaluate literature, identify research gaps, and develop well-organized research problems, objectives, and hypotheses. The primary focus will be on the acquisition of fundamental research skills, such as effective proposal writing, academic writing, and citation management. Additionally, students will improve their capacity to communicate research findings through structured oral presentations, technical reports, and scientific publications, in accordance with engineering communication standards. Upon completion of the course, students will possess the necessary skills to confidently articulate their findings, analyze data systematically, and design and execute research projects, thereby preparing them for advanced research in their respective engineering fields.

name: ENGINEERING PROJECT MANAGEMENT
synopsis: This course provides an in-depth exploration of project management principles tailored for engineering applications. It covers essential topics such as project planning, scheduling, budgeting, risk management, and quality assurance, with real-world case studies and industry best practices. Students will develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills to navigate complex engineering projects, ensuring efficiency, innovation, and sustainability. Through interactive discussions and practical applications, the course equips future engineering leaders with the tools needed to manage projects successfully in dynamic and evolving environments.

name: MACHINE LEARNING IN ENGINEERING
synopsis: This course introduces machine learning applications in engineering, focusing on predictive analytics, optimization, and automation in mechanical, energy, and industrial systems. Topics include data preprocessing, supervised and unsupervised learning, neural networks, and deep learning. The course also covers feature selection, model evaluation, and deployment of machine learning models in real-world engineering applications. Students will gain hands-on experience with Python-based machine learning tools for solving engineering challenges.

name: CRITICAL THINKING AND PROBLEM SOLVING SKILLS
synopsis: This course is aimed at developing and improving the student's thinking abilities such as clarifying and interpreting of ideas, detecting fallacies as well as analyzing and evaluating arguments. In this course, problem solving and decision making techniques will be taught to help students make informed decisions. In order to improve the students' communication, leadership skills and group skills as well as various techniques are also introduced through video presentations and discussions.

name: ARABIC LANGUAGE INFLUENCE ON MALAY LANGUAGE
synopsis: This course discusses the Arabic language influence on Malay language from the aspect of phonetics, semantics and writing. From the aspect of phonetics, the emphasis is placed on the absorbed sounds of the Arabic language and their changes in Malay language. From the aspect of semantics, the discussion focuses on the widening and narrowing of meaning. Moreover, focus is also rendered to the aspect of writing through the comparison between the original writing of Arabic words and their writing in Malay language.

name: MALAY LANGUAGE AND CULTURE
synopsis: This course introduces to students about the basic language and Malay culture. Besides that to exposed them the cultural diversity in Malay community. These include food, clothing, festivals, dance, musical instruments, architecture as well as influences and taboos in Malay society.

name: TECHNOLOGY IN LANGUAGE LEARNING
synopsis: This course aims to give students a broad overview of technology-enhanced language learning. Students will explore a working theory of language learning environments, use and discuss potential applications of computer technology in the language classroom, and create a project that demonstrates knowledge of technology application in language learning. In addition, the course will also address issues related to the use of technology in language learning in a variety of educational contexts.

name: ELEMENTARY ARABIC
synopsis: This course exposes Arabic sound and writing systems. Emphasis is given on writing and reading activities such as understanding, translation and so forth. Students are also trained to speak using simple sentences on topics related to the daily lives of Malaysians such as personal information, residence, acquaintance and so on. They are also exposed to elementary Arabic grammar in which they use in language activities.

name: BASIC JAPANESE LANGUAGE
synopsis: In this course, students will be exposed to basic Japanese language structures and the Japanese language system. Students will be taught skills in speaking and writing. They will learn to produce simple dialogues and sentences used in the Japanese culture. They will also be taught the correct pronunciation and intonation of the Japanese language.

name: BASIC GERMAN LANGUAGE
synopsis: In this course, students will be taught the four language skills at the basic level of A1. They will learn simple speech acts, listen, write and read and interpret sentences and short texts (e.g. personal letters, compositions and dialogues). They will also learn how to communicate effectively in simple everyday situations.

name: BASIC KOREAN LANGUAGE
synopsis: In this course, students will be exposed to basic Korean language structures and the Korean language system. Students will be taught skills in speaking and writing. They will learn to produce simple dialogues and sentences used in the Korean culture. They will also be taught the correct pronunciation and intonation of the Korean language. In addition, this course also briefly introduces the use of Korean in Malaysia

name: ELEMENTARY MALAY
synopsis: This course emphasises mastering basic skills in Malay for international students enrolled in the undergraduate study programmes. The course includes four skills, which are pronunciation and speaking; listening, reading and writing in Malay for basic communication. Emphasis is given to oral and written exercises.

Focus is on building speaking and reading competence with an emphasis on accuracy in grammar and on vocabulary building. Students will develop structural accuracy, reasonable oral fluency and language appropriateness by practising the language in a variety of contexts.

Students will be exposed to a variety of reading texts in order to improve their reading skills. Students will also be given ample speaking practice to develop their confidence in communicating and interacting with others in a multitude of situations. The course will also improve students’ basic skills in writing sentences and paragraphs.

Students will also be exposed to different communication strategies to enable them to interact effectively and communicate with clarity in collaborative discussions.

name: Basic Vietnamese Language 1
synopsis: This course introduced basic structures and grammar systems in Vietnamese language. Students will be taught reading, writing, listening and speaking skills. They will also learn to produce simple dialogues and sentences in Vietnamese language.

name: BAHASA MELAYU KOMUNIKASI
synopsis: This course trains international students to communicate in basic Malay, covering everyday life situations. Students will be introduced to simple spoken and written Malay. Teaching and learning will be conducted through tutorials, assignments, and students' learning experiences inside and outside the classroom. By the end of this course, students are expected to communicate and write effectively using simple sentences.

name: COMMUNICATION SKILLS FOR EMPLOYMENT PURPOSES
synopsis: This course introduces students to communication for employment purposes. Students will be familiarised with the various aspects involved in the process of obtaining a job such as producing effective resumes and email application letters. Students will also learn skills to perform successfully at job interviews. Students will also have the opportunity to obtain real world information regarding communication for employment purposes. This involves research skills to obtain information suitable for the field of work they are interested in.

name: CHINESE LANGUAGE AND CULTURE
synopsis: This course introduces the basic structure of Chinese language to the students, besides the cultural element in the usage of Chinese language. They are also exposed to the variety of Chinese cultural elements and usage of Chinese language, such as names of things, seasons, festivals, diets, numbers and colours. Students are also trained to communicate to use the basic structure of Chinese language and culture related to greetings, calls, prohibitions and so on.

name: JOURNALISM FOR SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT
synopsis: This course is designed for students interested in media communication of sustainability issues. The course introduces students to key concepts of sustainability, within the framework of the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals, challenges in sustainable reporting, as well as the principles and practices for holistic reporting of issues related to the environment, sustainability and development. In addition to conceptual knowledge, students will develop the ability to assess media reports for weaknesses in reporting sustainability. Students’ communication skills will also be developed through a variety of tasks, including group presentations, discussions and written reports.

name: ARABIC LANGUAGE ENRICHMENT AND LANGUAGE STYLE
synopsis: This course discusses the meaning of popular vocabulary and language styles in various fields related to daily life, religion, education, career, socio-culture, health, sports, administration, politics and economics. Students are trained in the vocabulary and language styles learned in writing and speaking with correct grammar.

name: READING AND WRITING 1
synopsis: This course trains students to read Arabic texts and write essays at intermediate level (CEFR level B2) in different fields such as religion, education, socio-cultural, health and sports. Emphasis is given to the reading of Arabic texts in terms of vocabulary, content, grammar and balaghah aspects. Besides that, students will be trained to write essays using the correct Arabic grammar structures.

name: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1
synopsis: This course trains students in intermediate listening skills (CEFR level B2) by responding to text that is heard in relation to their life and environment. Students are also trained in guided and one-way speaking activities such as storytelling, monologues, ceremony reading and so on. In addition, students carry out independent and two-way communication activities such as daily conversations, interviews, meetings and so on. In conducting such activities the emphasis is placed on the correct use of Arabic grammar and style

name: ARABIC LANGUAGE FOR MEDIA AND IT
synopsis: This course discusses the terms, meanings and the Arabic style related to media and IT covering various fields such as print media, audiovisual media, computers, the internet and more. Students are trained to use these terms and styles in writing and speaking activities in a various of situations. In carrying out of this activity, emphasis is given to the use of the exact meaning and correct grammar.

name: FUNCTIONAL GRAMMAR 1
synopsis: This course explains concepts and categories of Arabic nouns and verbs such as mu'rab, mabni, ma'rifah, nakirah and more. At the end of each topic, students are trained and tested on their understanding through the analysis and application of the features of nouns and verbs learnt

name: ARABIC LANGUAGE FOR COMMUNICATION AND TOURISM
synopsis: This course discusses the terms, meanings and styles of Arabic language related to communication and tourism covering various areas such as communication in personal contexts, careers, protocols, sports tourism, cultural tourism, historical tourism and more. Students are trained to use these terms and styles in writing and speaking activities in a variety of situations. In carrying out of this activity, emphasis is given to the use of the exact meaning and correct grammar.

name: DIALECTS AND READINGS
synopsis: This course discusses the history and features of ancient Arabic dialects, in the days of jahiliyah and the beginning of Islam in terms of sound, word construction and verse, and the meaning of words. The discussion also includes on the form of the Qira'at al-Qur'an and its connection with ancient Arabic dialects. In addition, students are exposed to modern Arabic dialects and their features in terms of pronunciation, vocabulary and sentence structure.

name: FUNCTIONAL MORPHOLOGY 2
synopsis: This course discusses the concepts, patterns and meanings of the Sarfi verbs and nouns in the categories of mu’tal thulathi including mujarad and mazid such as fi'il madhi, mudhari ', amar, masdar, isim fail, isim maf'ul and more. At the end of each topic, students are trained and tested on their understanding through the analysis and application of the features of nouns and verbs learned in reading and writing activities.

name: FUNCTIONAL GRAMMAR 3
synopsis: This course discusses secondary structures in Arabic language such as al-badal, al-taukid, al-maf'ul fih and more. At the end of each topic, students are trained and tested on their understanding through the analysis and application of the features of nouns and verbs learnt in reading and writing activities.

name: FUNCTIONAL GRAMMAR 4
synopsis: This course discusses Arabic grammar uslub such as madh wa zamm, uslub syarat, uslub ta’ajjub and more. At the end of each topic, students are trained and tested on their understanding through the analysis and application of the features of nouns and verbs learned in reading and writing activities.

name: ARABIC LANGUAGE FOR RELIGION AND EDUCATION
synopsis: This course discusses Arabic terms and meanings as well as Arabic language related to religion and education covering various fields such as Quran al-Karim, Hadith, worship, munakahat, muamalat, spiritual education, morals, children's education and so on. Students are trained to use these terms and styles in writing and speaking activities in a variety of situations. In carrying out of this activity, emphasis is given to the use of the exact meaning and correct grammar.

name: MA’ANI
synopsis: This course introduces the concept of ilmu ma'ani and its field of study as well as explain its relevance with pragmatic. Emphasis is given to the types and elements of sentences such as, al-musnad and al-musnad ilaih, al-uslub al-khabari and al-insya'i, al-ta'rif and al-tankir, al-taqdim and al-ta'khir and more. This course also trains students to apply the ilmu ma'ani in writing, including constructing sentences according to the context.

name: ARABIC & MIDDLE EASTERN LANGUAGES
synopsis: This course introduces the concept of ilmu bayan and its field of study. Emphasis is given to the variations of phrases and their suitability in the context such as al-hakikah and al-majaz, al-tasybih, al-isti‘arah andal-kinayah and so on. This course also trains students to apply the ilmu bayan in writing, including constructing sentences according to the context.

name: TWO WAYS TRANSLATION ARABIC-MALAY 1
synopsis: This course explains the concepts, theories, types, methods and techniques of translation generally. In addition, this course identifies the problems and issues faced in the process of Arabic text translation to Malay and vice versa. Emphasis is given to the implementation of the activities of the Arabic text translation into Malay and vice versa in the fields of religion, education, and social based on the theory and method of translation learned.

name: ARABIC LEXICOGRAPHY AND SEMANTIC
synopsis: This course introduces students to the concepts, scope and history of Arabic lexicografpy studies. They are trained to apply searching for the meaning of Arabic vocabulary according to/based on the method of Arabic lexicography. Students are also exposed to semantic concepts and theories in Arabic contexts such as context theory, lexical theory and so on.

name: ARABIC LANGUAGE LEARNING IN TECHNOLOGY
synopsis: This course introduces the concept of learning using technology applications that incorporate hardware, software, art of use and control in learning Arabic. Students are trained to use e-learning hardware and software especially electronic or internet based such as Socrative Quizzes, Digital Dialects, Duolingo and others in increasing Arabic proficiency. They/Students are also required to produce projects in Arabic using the technology learned.

name: LINGUISTICS OF AL-QURAN AND HADITH
synopsis: This course introduces the forms of i’jaz language in the Quranic texts and Hadith. Emphasis is given to the various features of sarf and grammar in both sources such as gender, number, uniformity and so on. This course also discusses the implied meaning of the language style and rethoric in the Quran al-Karim and Hadith, such as khabariy, insha'i and so on.

name: FUNCTIONAL MORPHOLOGY 3
synopsis: This course discusses the concepts and changes that apply to the structure of Arabic words related to i'lal, ibdal, idgham, and iltiqa 'al-sakinain. At the end of each topic, students are trained and tested on their understanding through the analysis and application of the features of nouns and verbs learned in reading and writing activities.

name: BADI’
synopsis: This course introduces the concept of ilmu badi’ and its field of study. Emphasis is given to the explanation of elements of wondrous/beauty sentences and their suitability in the context such as the beauty of words and the beauty of meaninfg. This course also trains students to apply the ilmu badi’ in writing, including constructing sentences according to the context.

name: ARABIC DISCOURSE ANALYSIS
synopsis: This course discusses the discourses in various Arabic-language texts including prose and poetry such as Quranic al-Karim, Hadiths, speeches, literature, technical and so on. Emphasis is given to the analysis of discourse features of each text learned from the aspects of textuality, grammatical discourse and lexical such as modality, coherence, cohesion, discourse markers and so on. Students are also trained to build the text by using discourse learned.

name: HISTORY OF GRAMMATICAL AND RHETORIC
synopsis: This course introduces the history and development of Arabic grammar and rhetoric in various eras and streams such as Basrah, Kufah and others. Students are exposed to the contributions of Arabic scholar in grammar and rhetoric and their work. Also discussed some of the selected main references in Arabic grammar and rhetoric.

name: ARABIC PHONETICS AND PHONOLOGY
synopsis: This course discusses phonetic concepts and its fields of study in the Arabic context such as consonants, vowels and so on. This course also discusses the phonological concepts and its fields of study and the differences between phonetics in the Arabic context as well as its areas of study such as the change of sound, nabr, tanghim and so on. Students are also exposed to the relation between the disciplines of phonetic and phonological with the discipline of tajwid.

name: KOREAN LANGUAGE SKILLS LEVEL I
synopsis: In this course, students will be exposed to basic Korean language structures and grammar system. Students will be taught reading, writing, listening and speaking skills. They will learn the correct pronunciation and intonation of the Korean language. They will also learn to produce simple dialogues and sentences used in the Korean language.

name: KOREAN LANGUAGE AND TOURISM
synopsis: In this course, students will be exposed to the use of Korean language in the professional fields of communication and tourism. Authentic material such as newspaper articles, magazines, journals, reports, formal letters, and media sources are used to reinforce the students’ understanding of language in tourism sector. The students will be given oral and written exercises.

name: INTRODUCTION TO COMMUNICATION IN GERMAN LANGUAGE LEVEL I
synopsis: In this course, students will be exposed to basic German language structures and grammar system. Students will be taught reading, writing, listening and speaking skills. They will learn the correct pronunciation and intonation of the German language. They will also learn to produce simple dialogues and sentences used in the German language.

name: INTRODUCTION TO COMMUNICATION IN ITALIAN LANGUAGE LEVEL I
synopsis: In this course, students will be exposed to basic Italian language structures and grammar system. Students will be taught reading, writing, listening and speaking skills. They will learn the correct pronunciation and intonation of the Italian language. They will also learn to produce simple dialogues and sentences used in the Italian language.

name: INTRODUCTION TO COMMUNICATION IN FRENCH LANGUAGE LEVEL I

They will learn the correct pronunciation and intonation of the French language. They will also learn to produce simple dialogues and sentences used in the French language.

They will learn the correct pronunciation and intonation of the Spanish language. They will also learn to produce simple dialogues and sentences used in the Spanish language.

name: INTRODUCTION TO COMMUNICATION IN KOREAN LANGUAGE LEVEL I
synopsis: This course introduced basic structures and grammar system in Korean language. Students will be taught reading, writing, listening and speaking skills. They will also learn to produce simple dialogues and sentences in Korean language.

name: INTRODUCTION TO COMMUNICATION IN PORTUGUESE LANGUAGE LEVEL I
synopsis: In this course, students will be exposed to basic Portuguese language structures and grammar system. Students will be taught reading, writing, listening and speaking skills. They will learn the correct pronunciation and intonation of the Portuguese language. They will also learn to produce simple dialogues and sentences used in the Portuguese language.

name: INTRODUCTION TO COMMUNICATION IN THAI LANGUAGE LEVEL I
synopsis: This course introduced basic structures and grammar system in Thai language. Students will be taught reading, writing, listening and speaking skills. They will also learn to produce simple dialogues and sentences in Thai language.

name: ELEMENTARY ARABIC LANGUAGE 1
synopsis: This course introduces the writing and sound system of Arabic letters in the context of single letters and words. Emphasis is given to language skills activities, especially reading and speaking skills at the basic level about self introduction, family, Arabic learning and it’s related situations. Students are also exposed to the basic Arabic grammar related to the simple words and sentences and they are trained to use it in language activities.

name: INTRODUCTION TO COMMUNICATION IN FILIPINO LANGUAGE LEVEL I
synopsis: This course introduced basic structures and grammar system in Filipino language. Students will be taught reading, writing, listening and speaking skills. They will also learn to produce simple dialogues and sentences in Filipino language.

name: INTRODUCTION TO COMMUNICATION IN VIETNAMESE LANGUAGE LEVEL I
synopsis: This course introduced basic structures and grammar system in Vietnamese language. Students will be taught reading, writing, listening and speaking skills. They will also learn to produce simple dialogues and sentences in Vietnamese language.

name: LANGUAGE AND GENDER
synopsis: This course introduces students to the aspects of language and gender differences, the role of hierarchical relationships in conversations, communication styles that take place in a 'public' and 'private' context. This course also examines how linguistic features, power and solidarity as well as culture affect the speech styles of its users.

name: LANGUAGE DISORDERS
synopsis: This course provides an introduction to the different types of language disorders. The students will have the opportunity to collaboratively collect linguistic data that show evidence of one or more types of disorder. Authentic data from individual persons with disabilities (PWDs) will be analysed to discuss the implications of language disorders in the local community.

name: INTRODUCTION TO COMMUNICATION IN ITALIAN LANGUAGE LEVEL II
synopsis: This course is the continuation of Introduction to Communication in Italian Language Level I. At this level, students will be exposed to basic Italian language structures and language system. Students will be taught in reading, writing, listening and speaking skills. They will learn the correct pronunciation and intonation of the Italian language. They also will be taught to state the correct verbs in different tenses and to respond by using simple dialogues and sentences.

name: INTRODUCTION TO COMMUNICATION IN SPANISH LANGUAGE LEVEL II
synopsis: This course is the continuation of Introduction to Communication in Spanish Language Level I. At this level, students will be exposed to basic Spanish language structures and language system. Students will be taught in reading, writing, listening and speaking skills. They will learn the correct pronunciation and intonation of the Spanish language. They also will be taught to state the correct verbs in different tenses and to respond by using simple dialogues and sentences.

name: INTRODUCTION TO COMMUNICATION IN KOREAN LANGUAGE LEVEL II
synopsis: This course is a continuation of Introduction to Communication in Korean Language Level I. At this level, students will be exposed to basic structures and language system in Korean anguage. Students will be taught further in reading, writing, listening and speaking skills . This course also includes the use of the correct form of verbs in different tenses.

name: INTRODUCTION TO COMMUNICATION IN THAI LANGUAGE LEVEL II
synopsis: This course is a continuation of Introduction to Communication in Thai Language Level I. At this level, students will be exposed to basic structures and language system in Thai language. Students will be taught further in reading, writing, listening and speaking skills . This course also includes the use of the correct form of verbs in different tenses.

name: AN INSIGHT INTO GERMAN LANGUAGE AND CULTURE
synopsis: This course uses multimedia resources as a starting point to present and discuss culture and language for German society. Along with traditional lectures the students are required to participate actively in class discussion on a wide range of topics about the tradition and culture of German, as well as on the comparison between German and students’ own culture. Students are also required to work in group for the final project which is related to German culture and society.

name: AN INSIGHT INTO ITALIAN LANGUAGE AND CULTURE
synopsis: This course uses multimedia resources as a starting point to present and discuss culture and language for Italian society. Along with traditional lectures, the students are required to participate actively in class discussion on a wide range of topics about the tradition and culture of Italy, as well as on the comparison between Italy and students’ own culture. Students are also required to work in groups for the final project which is related to Italian culture and society.

Along with traditional lectures, the students are required to participate actively in class discussion on a wide range of topics about the tradition and culture of French , as well as on the comparison between French and students’ own culture. Students are also required to work in group for the final project which is related to French culture and society.

name: AN INSIGHT INTO SPANISH LANGUAGE AND CULTURE
synopsis: This course uses multimedia resources as a starting point to introducing students to Spanish culture and language. Besides accessing online resources and attending traditional lectures, students will have opportunities to participate in class discussions and presentations on a variety of topics pertaining to Spanish culture and traditions. The course encourages students to engage in critical thinking through learning about and comparing Spanish and their own culture. Students are also required to work in group for the final project which is related to Spanish culture and society.

name: AN INSIGHT INTO KOREAN LANGUAGE AND CULTURE
synopsis: This course uses multimedia resources as a starting point to present and discuss culture and language for Korean society. Along with traditional lectures, the students are required to participate actively in class discussion on a wide range of topics about the tradition and culture of Korean, as well as on the comparison between Korea and students’ own culture. Students are also required to work in group for the final project which is related to Korea culture and society.

name: AN INSIGHT INTO THAI LANGUAGE AND CULTURE

name: AN INSIGHT INTO VIETNAMESE LANGUAGE AND CULTURE
synopsis: This course uses multimedia resources as a starting point to present and discuss culture and language for Vietnamese society. Along with traditional lectures, the students are required to participate actively in class discussion on a wide range of topics about the tradition and culture of Vietnamese, as well as on the comparison between Vietnam and Malaysia. Students are also required to work in group for the final project which is related to Vietnamese culture and society.

name: APPROACHES TO DISCOURSE ANALYSIS
synopsis: This course exposes students to the social production of meaning in discourse studies through a survey of the main strands in contemporary discourse analysis. Students will be taught the theoretical knowledge and empirical tools of various approaches to the analysis of discourse. Finally, the course aims to prepare students to carry out research using discourse analytical methods.

name: MULTILINGUALISM
synopsis: The course examines the concept of multilinguality in the Malaysian and regional contexts. Among the topics covered in this course include how multiple languages are practised in different contexts. The course also exposes students to practical skills in analysing data related to aspects of multilingualism.

name: TRANSLATION STUDIES
synopsis: This course introduces translation as a bilingual communication process involving different cultural and social contexts. Among the aspects explored are: (the strategies to solve translational challenges, the concept of equivalence, functionalist/skopos theory, the approaches of domestication and foreignization in translation; the use of technology in translation and; criteria for evaluating translation quality in different text types.

name: PRAGMATICS
synopsis: The course focuses on language use in cultural contexts, particularly how meaning is constructed and communicated. The aim of this course is to discuss major pragmatic theories and their practical application to the analysis of empirical data as well as the latest developments in pragmatics. The final part of the course trains students to integrate theoretical principles in conducting research and to produce a project paper.

name: LANGUAGE FOR SPECIFIC PURPOSES
synopsis: This course introduces students to the current theories and practices related to the planning of a Language for Specific Purposes (LSP) training programme for a group of target learners. Students are exposed to genre analysis among others as a research approach to critically examine the structure of various texts and discourses used in both the academic and professional settings. An interactive and practical approach, incorporating group discussions, case study, and presentations, is applied enabling students to carry out a needs analysis and design an LSP/ESP training programme for any organization. Students will also prepare a proposal of the training programme that they design.

name: MULTIMODAL STUDIES
synopsis: This course introduces students to the various concepts, theories and approaches in multimodal research. Students will explore how meaning making is a social practice in all modes of communication. Students will be also taught how to analyse various multimodal texts using different approaches.

name: CRITICAL DISCOURSE STUDIES
synopsis: This course introduces students to principles and approaches to critical discourse analysis. It aims to provide students with the theoretical knowledge and analytical tools that will enable them to investigate issues of social significance. The focus is on examining the different ways discourse is connected to hidden agenda, power and ideology.

name: METHODOLOGY IN ENGLISH LANGUAGE STUDIES
synopsis: TBD

name: ACADEMIC WRITING FOR ENGLISH STUDIES
synopsis: This course provides practical training in academic writing. The general approach of this course is analytical and rhetorical. Students will develop skills for analysing the structure and the rhetorical and linguistic features of effective academic writing. They will use these skills in their own writing. The tasks and activities in this course are richly varied ranging from language analysis to issues of what makes successful academic writing. By the end of this course, students will have mastered the key characteristics of academic English and developed a range of academic skills and writing strategies.

name: STRUCTURE OF ENGLISH
synopsis: This course aims to provide students with an understanding of the way English is constructed, which includes sounds, formation of words and structure of sentences, as well as meaning of words and sentences. Students will explore the basic terms, concepts and approaches related to the study of English sounds, word formation, structure and meaning. Through the use of examples from contemporary English, including different varieties of English, students will be able to distinguish differences in English language structure in speech and writing as well as English in different contexts. Concurrently, the relationships between them (e.g. sounds and word formation, sentence structure and meaning) will also be examined. The knowledge and skills gained in this course will aid students in their analyses of particular spoken and written contexts and varieties of English, not just in this course but in the programme of study as a whole.

synopsis: The course is divided into two: (1) A rough outline of Malaysian Legal history; and (2) Sources of Malaysian Law. In part (1) lies a historical out look of the legal history covering both the periods before and after the arrival of the British. In part (2) the sources

name: INTERNATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL LAW: NATURAL WORLD ISSUES
synopsis: This course examines the role of international law in addressing global environmental issues and problems, with regards to major global environmental issues and problems pertaining to Natural World issues. It addresses major legal environmental principles, concepts, duties and obligations relating to such phenomena. It also aims to evaluate the effectiveness of international environmental law in terms of its implementation and enforceability and compliance perspectives. Specific topics are examined under international environmental treaties and conventions and protocols such as CITES, RAMSAR, CBD, ITTA, etc providing for a diverse overview of global environmental issues, problems and challenges in the 21st century impacting Natural World issues . The interface between international and domestic environmental law -Implementation, compliance and enforcement of international environmental law are scrutinised and assessed in view of real case law and country studies with special focus on natural world dimension.

name: THE LAW OF THE SEA
synopsis: This course is based on the edifice of public international law. It discusses the evolution of the law of the sea at international law and identifies the main principles of the law of the sea under the 1982 Law of the Sea Convention and thereafter proceeds to examine the national laws on the seas and evaluates both the international and national regimes on the law of the sea.

name: INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY LAW
synopsis: This course focuses on the legal, policy, regulatory and governance issues concerning the Internet and applications of information technology. The approach is national, regional, international and comparative' in nature. Issues to be discussed and examined include internet governance, electronic commerce, privacy and data protection, cybercrime, and emerging technologies such as big data, cloud computing, Internet of Things (IoT) and Internet of Everything (loET) and Artificial Intelligence will be deliberated.

name: MEDIATION AND NEGOTIATION
synopsis: This course will introduce to two alternative methods, i.e. mediation and negotiation, to resolving disputes without resorting to the courts, negotiation theories and practical training to conduct negotiations, mediation techniques and theories and skills training to become a mediator.

name: ADVANCED EMPLOYMENT LAW
synopsis: The course examines the existing legal mechanisms in the field of Employment Law and assesses their effectiveness in safeguarding and promoting the rights and interests of employees at the workplace; in light of current legal as well as policy developments.

synopsis: This course is designed for students to gain advanced knowledge and skills related to public international law and practice, particularly in and from Asia-Pacific and Global South contexts and perspectives.

name: LAW AND ECONOMICS
synopsis: The course is designed to introduce students to selected topics in the area of law and economics. The topics include introduction to microeconomics, the economic theory of property law, the economy theory of tort law, the economic theory of contract law, and the economic theory of crime and punishment.

name: ARBITRATION LAW
synopsis: The course will consider the various aspects of the law governing domestic and international arbitrations. In this regard, the provisions of the Arbitration Act 2005 will be examined. Relevant international instruments will be introduced.

name: COPYRIGHT LAW
synopsis: The focus of this course is on the understanding of basic copyright concepts and Malaysian copyright law as found in the Copyright Act 1987. International developments in copyright and their impact on our law will also will be examined. This course will also cover specific issues such as those arising from developments in case law and technology.

name: CARRIAGE OF GOODS BY SEA
synopsis: This course covers carriage of goods by sea contracts recorded either in charterparties or in bills of lading, using a practical approach to look at the whole aspect of carriage of goods by sea from the fixing of the contract, the provision of the vessel, the shipping of the goods, the issue of documents, the voyage, to the discharge of the goods and the remedies.

name: CAPITAL MARKET LAW
synopsis: Capital markets and the laws governing them globally are constantly evolving due to the needs of businesses, innovative financial engineering and the investment needs of investors. In Malaysia, the last 15 years have witnessed a host of changes in the legal and regulatory framework of the securities and futures markets culminating in the passage of the Capital Markets and Services Act 2007. This course examines the main law and regulations relating to the Capital markets in Malaysia. This includes the Conventional and Islamic Capital Market. It also explores key issues with respect to securities transactions. This course will be broken up in the following parts: Part I will be on the Capital markets in general, while Part 2 will focus on the Islamic Capital Market.

name: CONSUMER PROTECTION LAW
synopsis: This course is to provide students with the theoretical as well as the practical aspects of consumer protection law. This course comprises of three main areas: (1) Consumer protection law in the aspects of misleading and deceptive conduct, false representation and unfair practices, unfair contract; consumer rights against supply of goods and services, safety of goods and services, remedy scheme of consumer protection law, regulatory bodies and enforcement. (2) Statutory approaches of Consumer Protection Act 1999 based on theories and concept (3) Comparative consumer protection law among selected jurisdictions.

name: INTERNATIONAL TRADE LAW
synopsis: This course examines the legal framework governing international trade. The course focusses on the law of the World Trade Organisation. It examines the trade dispute settlement mechanism, principles and rules of international trade and the harmonization of national regulations

name: INTERNATIONAL COMMERCIAL TRANSACTIONS
synopsis: This course offers the student an opportunity to study not only the theory and principles of international commercial law but also the way international commerce operates. The focus is on the practical issues arising from the legal rules. The course is guided by the vision that the information society of the 21st century requires a fundamental re-definition of legal, commercial and personal skills, as well as a new global philosophy

Forensic Pathology In clinical forensic deals with all medico-legal problems of living persons. Forensic Pathology deals with cause of death, identification and manner of death, etc.

name: CRIMINAL LAW
synopsis: This course will study in detail the importance of the elements of criminal law both in civil and shariah. This is to enable students to have a better understanding of the relationship between the citizen and the state in the context of application of criminal law

name: LAW OF EVIDENCE
synopsis: The course is conducted mainly in a seminar form with minimal lectures. The course will discuss in detail certain expects of the law of evidence. The course will analyse the system in Islamic evidence followed by the system in Malaysia and the United States. Analysis will be made between the systems to enable students to evaluate the criminal justice system in Malaysia.

name: FORENSIC SCIENCE
synopsis: The course underlines the general principles of forensic science. The course will also discuss various diciplines of forensic science and its application to the principles of the criminal justice.

name: ADMINISTRATION OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE
synopsis: The course examines issues relevant to the administration of criminal justice in Malaysia. The course enables students to appreciate issues relevant to the administration of criminal justice. It covers theoretical foundations relating to models of criminal justice process, the notion of justice and the need of normative standards. The course also covers critical issues in criminal justice namely the governance of police, inquiry of death and criminal justice policies in Malaysia. Overall, the course encourages students to adopt critical and analytical outlook towards criminal justices practices and policies in Malaysia.

name: FORENSIC EVIDENCE
synopsis: The course will discuss the general principles of forensic evidence. The course will also discuss various diciplines of forensic science and its application to the principles of the criminal justice

name: HUMAN TRAFFICKING
synopsis: TBD

name: RESEARCH METHODS
synopsis: The aim of this course is to give basic knowledge on selected research methods in criminal justice such as doctrinal law, socio-legal and empirical. This course is aimed to enable students to prepare research proposal at the postgraduate level. This course gives basic foundation to understand and interpret criminal justice research as well as design, implement and evaluate research projects. The main emphasis begins from conceptualising problem statement, ethics and method of research together with collecting and analysing research data. It also provides basic understanding of the Malaysian legal system and legal research.

name: CRIME, CRIMINAL JUSTICE AND SOCIETY
synopsis: TBD

name: GENETICS AND DEVELOPMENTAL BIOLOGY
synopsis: This course is designed to extend student knowledge and understanding on the principles of genetics and the mechanisms of genetic diversity, including aspects of heredity, developmental biology, as well as theories on the origins of life, evolution and speciation.

name: HUMAN BODY SYSTEMS I
synopsis: This course is an introduction to the cells, tissues and organisation of the human organs from an integrative perspective.
